citations.quote:
Let $A$ and $B$ be nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces and let $\mathcal N:\mathcal L(A)\to\mathcal L(B)$ be a quantum channel as in [[def-qc-quantum-channel]]. Choose a finite-dimensional environment $E$ and a linear isometry $V:A\to B\otimes E$ such that

$$\mathcal N(X)=\operatorname{Tr}_E(VXV^*)$$

for every $X\in\mathcal L(A)$; such a dilation exists by [[thm-qc-finite-stinespring-dilation]]. The channel

$$\mathcal N^c(X):=\operatorname{Tr}_B(VXV^*)\in\mathcal L(E)$$

is the **complementary channel associated with this chosen dilation**. The partial trace $\operatorname{Tr}_B$ contracts the first factor of the ordered product $B\otimes E$ ([[def-qc-first-factor-partial-trace]]).

It is a quantum channel: reorder $B\otimes E$ to $E\otimes B$ by the finite wire-permutation unitary ([[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]], [[thm-qc-wire-permutation-is-unitary]]); the reordered $V$ is still an isometry, so tracing its second factor $B$ gives a channel by [[thm-qc-isometry-partial-trace-is-channel]].

For a density operator $\rho$ on $A$, choose a finite purification $|\psi\rangle\in A\otimes R$ with $\operatorname{Tr}_R|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|=\rho$ ([[def-qc-ensemble-and-purification]]), and define $\omega_{BR}:=(\mathcal N\otimes\operatorname{id}_R)(|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|)$. Its **coherent information** from $A$ to $B$ is

$$I_c(\rho,\mathcal N):=S(\mathcal N(\rho))-S(\omega_{BR}),$$

where $S$ is finite-dimensional von Neumann entropy in nats ([[def-it-von-neumann-entropy]]). The value does not depend on the chosen purification: after padding reference spaces, any two purifications differ by a unitary on $R$ ([[thm-qc-purification-existence-and-unitary-equivalence]]); applying $\mathcal N\otimes\operatorname{id}_R$ preserves that unitary relation. A unitary maps an orthonormal eigenbasis to an orthonormal eigenbasis with the same eigenvalues, so entropy is unchanged ([[thm-complex-spectral-theorem-for-normal-endomorphisms]]). Padding adds only zero eigenvalues, which do not contribute.

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, with the root convention that its inner product is linear in the first argument, and let $\rho$ be a density operator on $H$ ([[def-qc-density-operator]]). If $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_d$ are its eigenvalues counted with multiplicity, define its **von Neumann entropy** by

$$S(\rho):=-\operatorname{tr}(\rho\ln\rho):=-\sum_{j:\lambda_j>0}\lambda_j\ln\lambda_j.$$

The trace is the finite-dimensional endomorphism trace ([[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]), and the spectral definition makes the expression independent of the eigenbasis. The term for a zero eigenvalue is defined to be $0\ln0:=0$. The default unit is nats, using the natural logarithm ([[def-natural-logarithm]]); the entropy in bits is $S_2(\rho):=S(\rho)/\ln2$.

Let $H,K$ be finite-dimensional complex-inner-product spaces with the tensor-product convention of [[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]]. For every $\Psi\in H\otimes K$ there are an integer $r\ge0$, positive numbers $s_1,\ldots,s_r$, and orthonormal families $u_1,\ldots,u_r\in H$ and $v_1,\ldots,v_r\in K$ such that

$$\Psi=\sum_{j=1}^r s_j u_j\otimes v_j,\qquad \|\Psi\|^2=\sum_{j=1}^r s_j^2.$$

For $\Psi=0$ take $r=0$ and the empty sum. For any chosen ordered pair of orthonormal bases, the construction below obtains the $s_j$ as the positive singular values of the coefficient matrix of $\Psi$ in their ordered product basis.

For a finite bipartite state $\rho_{AB}$ on the ordered product $H_A\otimes H_B$, write $\rho_A=\operatorname{Tr}_B\rho_{AB}$ and $\rho_B=\operatorname{Tr}_A\rho_{AB}$, using the partial traces in [[def-qc-partial-trace]] and [[def-qc-first-factor-partial-trace]]. They are states by [[lem-it-partial-traces-of-a-state-are-states]]. Define

$$S(A)_\rho:=S(\rho_A),\qquad S(A\mid B)_\rho:=S(\rho_{AB})-S(\rho_B),\qquad I(A:B)_\rho:=S(\rho_A)+S(\rho_B)-S(\rho_{AB}).$$

For a finite tripartite state $\rho_{ABC}$ on the ordered product $H_A\otimes H_B\otimes H_C$, set $\rho_{AB}:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H_C}\rho_{ABC}$ after identifying the factors as $(H_A\otimes H_B)\otimes H_C$, and $\rho_{BC}:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H_A}\rho_{ABC}$ after identifying them as $H_A\otimes(H_B\otimes H_C)$. Let $P:H_A\otimes H_B\otimes H_C\to H_A\otimes H_C\otimes H_B$ be the wire permutation taking factor order $A,B,C$ to $A,C,B$ ([[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]], [[thm-qc-wire-permutation-is-unitary]]) whose unique adjoint $P^*$ exists by [[thm-adjoint-exists-and-is-unique-in-finite-dimension]], and set $\rho_{AC}:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H_B}(P\rho_{ABC}P^*)$, tracing out the last factor. Because $P$ is unitary, $P\rho_{ABC}P^*$ is a state: unitary conjugation preserves non-negativity by the adjoint identity ([[def-adjoint-of-a-linear-map-between-inner-product-spaces]], [[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]]) and preserves trace by cyclicity ([[thm-trace-of-ab-equals-trace-of-ba]]). Finally set $\rho_C:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H_B}\rho_{BC}$. All these marginals are density operators by applying [[lem-it-partial-traces-of-a-state-are-states]] after grouping factors. Define

$$I(A:B\mid C)_\rho:=S(\rho_{AC})+S(\rho_{BC})-S(\rho_C)-S(\rho_{ABC}).$$

These are finite-dimensional definitions only; no non-negativity of conditional entropy or conditional mutual information is part of the notation.

Let $\mathcal N:A\to B$ be a quantum channel between nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces, and fix any finite Stinespring complement $\mathcal N^c:A\to E$. Both functions

$$\rho\longmapsto I_c(\rho,\mathcal N),\qquad \rho\longmapsto S(\rho)+I_c(\rho,\mathcal N)$$

attain a maximum on the density operators on $A$.

For a finite-dimensional channel $\mathcal N:A\to B$, define

$$f_{\mathcal N}(\rho):=S(\rho)+I_c(\rho,\mathcal N),\qquad F(\mathcal N):=\sup_{\rho\in\mathcal D(A)}f_{\mathcal N}(\rho).$$

For any two finite-dimensional channels $\mathcal N_i:A_i\to B_i$,

$$F(\mathcal N_1\otimes\mathcal N_2)=F(\mathcal N_1)+F(\mathcal N_2).$$

Let $\tau=JJ^*/D$ be the flat state of a nonzero $D$-dimensional input subspace of a finite-dimensional channel $\mathcal N$. With prior shared maximally entangled states on that subspace, every $0\le R<S(\tau)+I_c(\tau,\mathcal N)$ is achievable for classical messages with average error tending to zero. The code consists of finite Weyl operations followed by a collective output/reference POVM; it has rate tending to $R$.

Let $\mathcal N:\mathcal L(A)\to\mathcal L(B)$ be a finite-dimensional channel, let $d=\dim A$, and let $\rho$ be a state on $A$. Fix a finite Stinespring dilation of $\mathcal N$ and its complementary channel. For each integer $n\ge1$ there is an exact decomposition $\rho^{\otimes n}=\sum_t p_t\tau_t$ into mutually orthogonal flat spectral-type states, with at most $(n+1)^d$ positive-weight types and $H(T):=-\sum_{t:p_t>0}p_t\ln p_t\le d\ln(n+1)$. For the fixed complement and its tensor powers, $$\sum_t p_t I_c(\tau_t,\mathcal N^{\otimes n})\ge nI_c(\rho,\mathcal N)-H(T),$$ $$\sum_t p_t[S(\tau_t)+I_c(\tau_t,\mathcal N^{\otimes n})]\ge n[S(\rho)+I_c(\rho,\mathcal N)]-2H(T).$$ Thus in each inequality some flat type state attains at least the displayed lower bound.

Let $\omega_{ZA}$ be any finite-dimensional state with $\operatorname{Tr}_Z\omega_{ZA}=\rho_A$, and let $|\psi\rangle_{RA}$ purify $\rho_A$ with $R$ a copy of $A$. There is a CPTP map $\Lambda:R\to Z$ with $(\Lambda\otimes\operatorname{id}_A)(|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|)=\omega_{ZA}$.

Let $A,B,A',B'$ be nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces, let $\rho_{AB}$ be a density operator on $A\otimes B$, and let $\Phi:A\to A'$ and $\Psi:B\to B'$ be quantum channels. Then

$$I(A':B')_{(\Phi\otimes\Psi)(\rho)}\le I(A:B)_\rho,$$

where quantum mutual information is $I(X:Y)_\omega=S(\omega_X)+S(\omega_Y)-S(\omega_{XY})$ as in [[def-it-finite-quantum-information-measures]].

Let $X$ take values in an alphabet $\mathcal X$ of size $m\ge2$, let $Y$ be finite, and let $\widehat X$ be an estimator in the same alphabet generated from $Y$, so the joint pmf factors as $p_{XY\widehat X}=p_{XY}p_{\widehat X|Y}$. Put $P_e=\mathbb P[\widehat X\ne X]$ and define

$$h_2(t):=-t\ln t-(1-t)\ln(1-t),\qquad 0\ln0:=0.$$

Then

$$H(X|Y)\le h_2(P_e)+P_e\ln(m-1)\le \ln2+P_e\ln m.$$

For $m=1$, $X$ is constant and $H(X|Y)=0$.

Let $X$ be a finite nonempty set, let $(p_x)$ be a probability vector, let $\rho_x$ be density operators on a nonzero finite-dimensional space $H_B$, and let $\bar\rho:=\sum_xp_x\rho_x$. For a finite POVM $(E_y)_{y\in Y}$ on $H_B$, define $w(y\mid x):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho_xE_y)$, $q_y:=\sum_xp_xw(y\mid x)$, and the classical mutual information

$$I(X:Y):=\sum_{x,y:p_xw(y\mid x)>0}p_xw(y\mid x)\ln\frac{w(y\mid x)}{q_y}.$$

Then

$$I(X:Y)\le\chi(\{p_x,\rho_x\})=S(\bar\rho)-\sum_{x:p_x>0}p_xS(\rho_x).$$

For finite $X,Y,Z$ with a joint pmf,

$$H(X,Y|Z)=H(X|Z)+H(Y|X,Z),$$

and

$$I(X;Y,Z)=I(X;Z)+I(X;Y|Z).$$

In particular, $I(X;Y)=H(X)-H(X|Y)=H(Y)-H(Y|X)$. All terms are finite.

The function $\log:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ is continuous and strictly increasing, is onto $\mathbb R$, and satisfies, for $x,y>0$,
$$\log(xy)=\log x+\log y,\qquad \log(x/y)=\log x-\log y,\qquad \log(1/x)=-\log x.$$
Also $\log 1=0$.

For every $\alpha>0$,
$$\lim_{x\to+\infty}\frac{\log x}{x^\alpha}=0.$$

Let $H_A,H_B,H_C$ be nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces and let $\rho_{ABC}$ be a density operator on their ordered tensor product. Write $\rho_{AB},\rho_{BC},\rho_B$ for its marginals using the partial traces in [[def-qc-partial-trace]]. Then
$$S(\rho_{AB})+S(\rho_{BC})\ge S(\rho_B)+S(\rho_{ABC}),$$
where $S(\rho)=-\operatorname{tr}(\rho\ln\rho)$ with $0\ln0:=0$ as in [[def-it-von-neumann-entropy]].

For a finite-dimensional bipartite state $\rho_{AB}$,

$$I(A:B)_\rho=S(\rho_A)+S(\rho_B)-S(\rho_{AB})=D(\rho_{AB}\|\rho_A\otimes\rho_B).$$

For a finite classical-quantum state $\rho_{XB}=\sum_xp_x\Pi_x\otimes\rho_x$, its mutual information equals its Holevo information:

$$I(X:B)_\rho=S\!\left(\sum_xp_x\rho_x\right)-\sum_{x:p_x>0}p_xS(\rho_x)=\chi(\{p_x,\rho_x\}).$$

derivations.claim: For any purification $\psi_{RA}$, its reference marginal is $\rho_R$ with the same positive eigenvalues as $\rho_A$, so $S(R)=S(\rho)$ by [F1]. Substituting [F1] into [F2] gives $I(R;B)=S(\rho)+I_c(\rho,\mathcal N)$. Thus the two maximized information expressions in the Statement agree, and [F3] supplies their maximizers.

By [F4], the optimized one-use information is additive across every finite tensor power; hence its regularized information value is the same one-use maximum. This proves additivity for the information expression itself.

For any input state $\rho$ and positive integer $m$, exact spectral type reduction gives a flat state $\tau_t$ on an $m$-use input subspace such that $$f_{\mathcal N^{\otimes m}}(\tau_t)\ge m f_{\mathcal N}(\rho)-2d\ln(m+1),\qquad d=\dim A.$$ Apply the flat-state construction to that fixed block channel. For fixed $m$, both its Weyl alphabet and its receiver output dimension are finite, so the HSW theorem applies before any limit in $m$ is taken. The shared resource is the flat type-subspace maximally entangled state for each outer block. Padding fewer than $m$ unused original-channel inputs with a fixed state gives codes for all sufficiently large lengths and no asymptotic rate loss. Therefore $$C_E(\mathcal N)\ge f_{\mathcal N}(\rho)-\frac{2d\ln(m+1)}m.$$ Since $\ln(m+1)/m\to0$ by [F13], letting $m\to\infty$ and maximizing over $\rho$ proves the general direct bound with precisely the stated unlimited finite-shared-entanglement model. No unrestricted quantum-input HSW single-letter theorem and no inference from Schumacher compression alone is used.

Consider any length-$n$ stated EA code with uniform message register $M$, receiver's prior share $S$, channel input $A^n$, and receiver output $B^nS$. Before transmission its joint state is $$\omega_{MA^nS}=\frac1K\sum_m|m\rangle\langle m|\otimes(\mathcal E_m\otimes\operatorname{id}_S)(\sigma).$$ The marginal $MS$ is the product of the uniform message and the original share: each encoder is trace-preserving and hence cannot change $S$. In particular $I(M:S)=0$. Let $\bar\rho_{A^n}$ be its average input. By the extension lemma, the $MSA^n$ state is obtained by a channel on the reference of a purification of $\bar\rho_{A^n}$. After transmission, quantum-mutual-information data processing gives $$I(MS:B^n)\le I(R:B^n)_{(\operatorname{id}\otimes\mathcal N^{\otimes n})(\psi_{\bar\rho})}.$$ Expanding the entropy definitions gives the exact identity $$I(M:B^nS)=I(MS:B^n)-I(S:B^n)+I(M:S).$$ The last term is zero, and [F14] gives $I(S:B^n)\ge0$. Therefore $$I(M:B^nS)\le I(R:B^n)\le F(\mathcal N^{\otimes n})=nF(\mathcal N).$$ The equality uses the stated optimized-information additivity lemma, whose proof follows local-channel mutual-information data processing and product-state entropy additivity. Write $h(u)=-u\ln u-(1-u)\ln(1-u)$ with continuous endpoint values. By [F11], $I(M;\widehat M)=H(M)-H(M\mid\widehat M)$; [F15] identifies $I(M:B^nS)$ with the Holevo quantity of the cq output state, and the Holevo measurement bound [F10] gives $I(M;\widehat M)\le I(M:B^nS)$. Fano then gives $$(1-e_n)\ln K_n\le nF(\mathcal N)+h(e_n).$$ Singleton message sets are trivial. Divide by $n$ and let average error tend to zero to bound every achievable rate by $F(\mathcal N)$, without restricting the shared state, its dimension, or the message-dependent CPTP encoders. Together with the general direct bound, purification identity and attained maximum, this proves the entire retained operational formula. Finally applying the identity $C_E=F$ to both channels and their product, and using the stated proved additivity of $F$, proves the capacity additivity assertion as well.

supplier_interfaces.excerpt:
Let $\mathcal N:A\to B$ be a finite-dimensional quantum channel and use its memoryless extension $\mathcal N^{\otimes n}:A^{\otimes n}\to B^{\otimes n}$. Rates use natural logarithms, so they are in nats per channel use. For code sizes $K_n\ge1$, a rate $R\ge0$ is achievable when $\liminf_{n\to\infty}n^{-1}\ln K_n\ge R$ and the relevant error terms below tend to zero; each capacity is the supremum of its achievable rates.

For **quantum transmission**, a block code consists of an isometric encoder $W_n:M_n\to A^{\otimes n}$ and a quantum-channel decoder $\mathcal D_n:B^{\otimes n}\to M_n$, where $\dim M_n=K_n$. Let $R_n\cong M_n$ and let $|\Phi_{K_n}\rangle\in R_n\otimes M_n$ be a normalized maximally entangled vector. Its entanglement fidelity is

$$F_n:=\langle\Phi_{K_n}|(\operatorname{id}_{R_n}\otimes\mathcal D_n\mathcal N^{\otimes n}\mathcal W_n)(|\Phi_{K_n}\rangle\langle\Phi_{K_n}|)|\Phi_{K_n}\rangle,$$

where $\mathcal W_n(X)=W_nXW_n^*$. A rate is quantum-achievable if $F_n\to1$; the resulting capacity is $Q(\mathcal N)$. This is the subspace entanglement-transmission convention.

For **private classical transmission**, a block code uses equiprobable messages $m\in[K_n]$, input states $\rho_{m,n}$ on $A^{\otimes n}$, and a decoding POVM $\{\Lambda_{m,n}\}_{m=1}^{K_n}$ on $B^{\otimes n}$. Its average error is

$$e_n:=1-\frac1{K_n}\sum_{m=1}^{K_n}\operatorname{tr}(\Lambda_{m,n}\mathcal N^{\otimes n}(\rho_{m,n})).$$

Fix a complementary channel $\mathcal N^c$ as in [[def-it-quantum-channel-complement-and-coherent-information]]. Eve's average state is $\bar\tau_n=K_n^{-1}\sum_m(\mathcal N^c)^{\otimes n}(\rho_{m,n})$. Define leakage by its Holevo information

$$\ell_n:=S(\bar\tau_n)-\frac1{K_n}\sum_{m=1}^{K_n}S((\mathcal N^c)^{\otimes n}(\rho_{m,n})).$$

A rate is privately achievable when $e_n\to0$ and $\ell_n\to0$; this is strong secrecy in mutual-information form. The corresponding capacity is $P(\mathcal N)$. The value is independent of the chosen complementary dilation, as follows from [[lem-it-private-information-is-coherent-information-difference]].

For **classical transmission with prior shared entanglement**, for each block length $n$ the sender and receiver begin with a finite-dimensional shared state $\sigma_{S_AS_B}$ independent of the equiprobable message. For each $m\in[K_n]$, the sender applies a quantum channel $\mathcal E_{m,n}:\mathcal L(S_A)\to\mathcal L(A^{\otimes n})$. The receiver measures $B^{\otimes n}\otimes S_B$ with a POVM $\{\Gamma_{m,n}\}_{m=1}^{K_n}$. Its average error is

$$e_n^{EA}:=1-\frac1{K_n}\sum_{m=1}^{K_n}\operatorname{tr}\!\left[\Gamma_{m,n}\bigl((\mathcal N^{\otimes n}\circ\mathcal E_{m,n})\otimes\operatorname{id}_{S_B}\bigr)(\sigma_{S_AS_B})\right].$$ A rate is achievable when this error tends to zero; there is no constraint on the dimension or consumption of the shared entanglement. The resulting capacity is $C_E(\mathcal N)$.

The input, output, and reference registers are finite-dimensional in each block. No single-letter formula is included in these operational definitions.

Let $A$ and $B$ be nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces and let $\mathcal N:\mathcal L(A)\to\mathcal L(B)$ be a quantum channel as in [[def-qc-quantum-channel]]. Choose a finite-dimensional environment $E$ and a linear isometry $V:A\to B\otimes E$ such that

$$\mathcal N(X)=\operatorname{Tr}_E(VXV^*)$$

for every $X\in\mathcal L(A)$; such a dilation exists by [[thm-qc-finite-stinespring-dilation]]. The channel

$$\mathcal N^c(X):=\operatorname{Tr}_B(VXV^*)\in\mathcal L(E)$$

is the **complementary channel associated with this chosen dilation**. The partial trace $\operatorname{Tr}_B$ contracts the first factor of the ordered product $B\otimes E$ ([[def-qc-first-factor-partial-trace]]).

It is a quantum channel: reorder $B\otimes E$ to $E\otimes B$ by the finite wire-permutation unitary ([[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]], [[thm-qc-wire-permutation-is-unitary]]); the reordered $V$ is still an isometry, so tracing its second factor $B$ gives a channel by [[thm-qc-isometry-partial-trace-is-channel]].

For a density operator $\rho$ on $A$, choose a finite purification $|\psi\rangle\in A\otimes R$ with $\operatorname{Tr}_R|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|=\rho$ ([[def-qc-ensemble-and-purification]]), and define $\omega_{BR}:=(\mathcal N\otimes\operatorname{id}_R)(|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|)$. Its **coherent information** from $A$ to $B$ is

$$I_c(\rho,\mathcal N):=S(\mathcal N(\rho))-S(\omega_{BR}),$$

where $S$ is finite-dimensional von Neumann entropy in nats ([[def-it-von-neumann-entropy]]). The value does not depend on the chosen purification: after padding reference spaces, any two purifications differ by a unitary on $R$ ([[thm-qc-purification-existence-and-unitary-equivalence]]); applying $\mathcal N\otimes\operatorname{id}_R$ preserves that unitary relation. A unitary maps an orthonormal eigenbasis to an orthonormal eigenbasis with the same eigenvalues, so entropy is unchanged ([[thm-complex-spectral-theorem-for-normal-endomorphisms]]). Padding adds only zero eigenvalues, which do not contribute.

For a finite bipartite state $\rho_{AB}$ on the ordered product $H_A\otimes H_B$, write $\rho_A=\operatorname{Tr}_B\rho_{AB}$ and $\rho_B=\operatorname{Tr}_A\rho_{AB}$, using the partial traces in [[def-qc-partial-trace]] and [[def-qc-first-factor-partial-trace]]. They are states by [[lem-it-partial-traces-of-a-state-are-states]]. Define

$$S(A)_\rho:=S(\rho_A),\qquad S(A\mid B)_\rho:=S(\rho_{AB})-S(\rho_B),\qquad I(A:B)_\rho:=S(\rho_A)+S(\rho_B)-S(\rho_{AB}).$$

For a finite tripartite state $\rho_{ABC}$ on the ordered product $H_A\otimes H_B\otimes H_C$, set $\rho_{AB}:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H_C}\rho_{ABC}$ after identifying the factors as $(H_A\otimes H_B)\otimes H_C$, and $\rho_{BC}:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H_A}\rho_{ABC}$ after identifying them as $H_A\otimes(H_B\otimes H_C)$. Let $P:H_A\otimes H_B\otimes H_C\to H_A\otimes H_C\otimes H_B$ be the wire permutation taking factor order $A,B,C$ to $A,C,B$ ([[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]], [[thm-qc-wire-permutation-is-unitary]]) whose unique adjoint $P^*$ exists by [[thm-adjoint-exists-and-is-unique-in-finite-dimension]], and set $\rho_{AC}:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H_B}(P\rho_{ABC}P^*)$, tracing out the last factor. Because $P$ is unitary, $P\rho_{ABC}P^*$ is a state: unitary conjugation preserves non-negativity by the adjoint identity ([[def-adjoint-of-a-linear-map-between-inner-product-spaces]], [[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]]) and preserves trace by cyclicity ([[thm-trace-of-ab-equals-trace-of-ba]]). Finally set $\rho_C:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H_B}\rho_{BC}$. All these marginals are density operators by applying [[lem-it-partial-traces-of-a-state-are-states]] after grouping factors. Define

$$I(A:B\mid C)_\rho:=S(\rho_{AC})+S(\rho_{BC})-S(\rho_C)-S(\rho_{ABC}).$$

These are finite-dimensional definitions only; no non-negativity of conditional entropy or conditional mutual information is part of the notation.

For a finite-dimensional channel $\mathcal N:A\to B$, define

$$f_{\mathcal N}(\rho):=S(\rho)+I_c(\rho,\mathcal N),\qquad F(\mathcal N):=\sup_{\rho\in\mathcal D(A)}f_{\mathcal N}(\rho).$$

For any two finite-dimensional channels $\mathcal N_i:A_i\to B_i$,

$$F(\mathcal N_1\otimes\mathcal N_2)=F(\mathcal N_1)+F(\mathcal N_2).$$

Let $\mathcal N:A\to B$ be a quantum channel between nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces, and fix any finite Stinespring complement $\mathcal N^c:A\to E$. Both functions

$$\rho\longmapsto I_c(\rho,\mathcal N),\qquad \rho\longmapsto S(\rho)+I_c(\rho,\mathcal N)$$

attain a maximum on the density operators on $A$.

Let $\rho$ be a density operator on a nonzero finite-dimensional source space, and use the squared entanglement-fidelity code model of [[def-it-quantum-source-and-compression-code]]. Write $S(\rho)$ in nats.

1. For every $R>S(\rho)$ there is a sequence of compression codes with $F_e^{(n)}\to1$ and $\limsup_n n^{-1}\ln M_n\le R$.
2. If a sequence of codes satisfies $\limsup_n n^{-1}\ln M_n<S(\rho)$, then $F_e^{(n)}\to0$.

Thus the asymptotic reliable compression rate is exactly $S(\rho)$ nats per source letter, or $S(\rho)/\ln2$ qubits per source letter.

Let $x\mapsto\rho_x$ be a finite-input, finite-output memoryless cq channel as in [[def-it-classical-quantum-memoryless-channel]]. With the average-error code convention of [[def-it-cq-channel-block-code-and-error]], its classical capacity in nats per use is
$$C_{\rm cq}=\max_{p\in\Delta(\mathcal X)}\chi_p,\qquad \chi_p:=S\!\left(\sum_xp_x\rho_x\right)-\sum_{x:p_x>0}p_xS(\rho_x).$$
For every $0\le R<C_{\rm cq}$ a sequence of codes with rate tending to $R$ has average error tending to zero, and every reliable sequence has limiting upper rate at most $C_{\rm cq}$. This theorem concerns a fixed finite classical input alphabet and does not assert a single-letter formula for general quantum-input channels.

Let $H,K$ be finite-dimensional complex-inner-product spaces with the tensor-product convention of [[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]]. For every $\Psi\in H\otimes K$ there are an integer $r\ge0$, positive numbers $s_1,\ldots,s_r$, and orthonormal families $u_1,\ldots,u_r\in H$ and $v_1,\ldots,v_r\in K$ such that

$$\Psi=\sum_{j=1}^r s_j u_j\otimes v_j,\qquad \|\Psi\|^2=\sum_{j=1}^r s_j^2.$$

For $\Psi=0$ take $r=0$ and the empty sum. For any chosen ordered pair of orthonormal bases, the construction below obtains the $s_j$ as the positive singular values of the coefficient matrix of $\Psi$ in their ordered product basis.

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, with the root convention that its inner product is linear in the first argument, and let $\rho$ be a density operator on $H$ ([[def-qc-density-operator]]). If $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_d$ are its eigenvalues counted with multiplicity, define its **von Neumann entropy** by

$$S(\rho):=-\operatorname{tr}(\rho\ln\rho):=-\sum_{j:\lambda_j>0}\lambda_j\ln\lambda_j.$$

The trace is the finite-dimensional endomorphism trace ([[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]), and the spectral definition makes the expression independent of the eigenbasis. The term for a zero eigenvalue is defined to be $0\ln0:=0$. The default unit is nats, using the natural logarithm ([[def-natural-logarithm]]); the entropy in bits is $S_2(\rho):=S(\rho)/\ln2$.

Let $\mathcal E_{d,\epsilon}$ be the finite-dimensional erasure channel with data dimension $d\ge1$ and erasure probability $\epsilon\in[0,1]$, with the complementary dilation in [[lem-it-qudit-erasure-channel-complement-and-degradability]]. For every input state $\rho$,

$$I_c(\rho,\mathcal E_{d,\epsilon})=(1-2\epsilon)S(\rho).$$

For $\mathcal E_{d,\epsilon}$, choose the Stinespring isometry in [[thm-it-qudit-erasure-channel-is-cptp]], with environment $E=A\oplus\mathbb C e_E$. Its complement is

$$\mathcal E^c_{d,\epsilon}(X)=\epsilon J_EXJ_E^*\oplus(1-\epsilon)\operatorname{tr}(X)|e_E\rangle\langle e_E|.$$

The channel is degradable for $0\le\epsilon\le\tfrac12$ and antidegradable for $\tfrac12\le\epsilon\le1$.

Let $\mathcal N:A\to B$ be a finite-dimensional degradable channel with a fixed complement $\mathcal N^c$. Then

$$Q(\mathcal N)=P(\mathcal N)=\max_{\rho\in\mathcal D(A)}I_c(\rho,\mathcal N),$$

and both regularizations in the quantum and private capacity formulas collapse to this one-use maximum.

Let $\mathcal N:A\to B$ be a finite-dimensional memoryless quantum channel. For $n\ge1$, put

$$q_n(\mathcal N):=\sup_{\rho\in\mathcal D(A^{\otimes n})}I_c(\rho,\mathcal N^{\otimes n}).$$

Under the subspace entanglement-transmission convention in [[def-it-quantum-channel-operational-capacities]],

$$Q(\mathcal N)=\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{q_n(\mathcal N)}n=\sup_{n\ge1}\frac{q_n(\mathcal N)}n.$$

No general single-letter or additivity assertion is made.

Let $\mathcal N:A\to B$ be a finite-dimensional memoryless quantum channel. For each $n\ge1$, let

$$p_n(\mathcal N):=\sup_{\mathcal E_n} I_p(\mathcal E_n,\mathcal N^{\otimes n}),$$

where the supremum ranges over all finite ensembles of input states on $A^{\otimes n}$. Under the strong-secrecy, average-error convention in [[def-it-quantum-channel-operational-capacities]],

$$P(\mathcal N)=\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{p_n(\mathcal N)}n=\sup_{n\ge1}\frac{p_n(\mathcal N)}n.$$

This statement is regularized and asserts no general single-letter formula.

Let $\mathcal N:A\to B$ be a finite-dimensional quantum channel. Under the shared-entanglement coding convention in [[def-it-quantum-channel-operational-capacities]],

$$C_E(\mathcal N)=\max_{\rho\in\mathcal D(A)}\bigl(S(\rho)+I_c(\rho,\mathcal N)\bigr)=\max_{\rho\in\mathcal D(A)}I(R;B)_{(\operatorname{id}_R\otimes\mathcal N)(\psi_\rho)},$$

where $\psi_\rho$ is any finite purification of $\rho$ on $R\otimes A$. The value is additive: $C_E(\mathcal N_1\otimes\mathcal N_2)=C_E(\mathcal N_1)+C_E(\mathcal N_2)$ for finite-dimensional channels.

Let $A,B,A',B'$ be nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces, let $\rho_{AB}$ be a density operator on $A\otimes B$, and let $\Phi:A\to A'$ and $\Psi:B\to B'$ be quantum channels. Then

$$I(A':B')_{(\Phi\otimes\Psi)(\rho)}\le I(A:B)_\rho,$$

where quantum mutual information is $I(X:Y)_\omega=S(\omega_X)+S(\omega_Y)-S(\omega_{XY})$ as in [[def-it-finite-quantum-information-measures]].

For a finite bipartite state $\rho_{AB}$ on the ordered product $H_A\otimes H_B$, write $\rho_A=\operatorname{Tr}_B\rho_{AB}$ and $\rho_B=\operatorname{Tr}_A\rho_{AB}$, using the partial traces in [[def-qc-partial-trace]] and [[def-qc-first-factor-partial-trace]]. They are states by [[lem-it-partial-traces-of-a-state-are-states]]. Define

$$S(A)_\rho:=S(\rho_A),\qquad S(A\mid B)_\rho:=S(\rho_{AB})-S(\rho_B),\qquad I(A:B)_\rho:=S(\rho_A)+S(\rho_B)-S(\rho_{AB}).$$

For a finite tripartite state $\rho_{ABC}$ on the ordered product $H_A\otimes H_B\otimes H_C$, set $\rho_{AB}:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H_C}\rho_{ABC}$ after identifying the factors as $(H_A\otimes H_B)\otimes H_C$, and $\rho_{BC}:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H_A}\rho_{ABC}$ after identifying them as $H_A\otimes(H_B\otimes H_C)$. Let $P:H_A\otimes H_B\otimes H_C\to H_A\otimes H_C\otimes H_B$ be the wire permutation taking factor order $A,B,C$ to $A,C,B$ ([[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]], [[thm-qc-wire-permutation-is-unitary]]) whose unique adjoint $P^*$ exists by [[thm-adjoint-exists-and-is-unique-in-finite-dimension]], and set $\rho_{AC}:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H_B}(P\rho_{ABC}P^*)$, tracing out the last factor. Because $P$ is unitary, $P\rho_{ABC}P^*$ is a state: unitary conjugation preserves non-negativity by the adjoint identity ([[def-adjoint-of-a-linear-map-between-inner-product-spaces]], [[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]]) and preserves trace by cyclicity ([[thm-trace-of-ab-equals-trace-of-ba]]). Finally set $\rho_C:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H_B}\rho_{BC}$. All these marginals are density operators by applying [[lem-it-partial-traces-of-a-state-are-states]] after grouping factors. Define

$$I(A:B\mid C)_\rho:=S(\rho_{AC})+S(\rho_{BC})-S(\rho_C)-S(\rho_{ABC}).$$

These are finite-dimensional definitions only; no non-negativity of conditional entropy or conditional mutual information is part of the notation.

Let $\mathcal N:A\to B$ be a finite-dimensional channel with chosen complement $\mathcal N^c:A\to E$, and let $\mathcal E=\{p_x,\rho_x\}_{x\in\mathcal X}$ be a finite ensemble on $A$ with $\bar\rho=\sum_xp_x\rho_x$. Then

$$I_p(\mathcal E,\mathcal N)=I_c(\bar\rho,\mathcal N)-\sum_{x:p_x>0}p_x I_c(\rho_x,\mathcal N).$$

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space of dimension $d$, and let $\rho$ be a density operator on $H$. Then

$$S(\rho)\le\ln d,$$

with equality if and only if $\rho=I_H/d$.

Let $\Phi:\mathcal L(H)\to\mathcal L(K)$ and
$\Psi:\mathcal L(K)\to\mathcal L(L)$ be finite-dimensional quantum channels.
Then $\Psi\circ\Phi$ is a channel. If
$\Theta:\mathcal L(H')\to\mathcal L(K')$ is another finite-dimensional
channel, the tensor map
$\Phi\otimes\Theta:\mathcal L(H\otimes H')\to\mathcal L(K\otimes K')$
is the linear map specified on product matrix units by
$(\Phi\otimes\Theta)(E_{uv}\otimes F_{st})=
\Phi(E_{uv})\otimes\Theta(F_{st})$. The basis result
[[lem-qc-tensor-products-of-operator-matrix-units-form-a-basis]] makes this
map well-defined and unique. It is also a channel, with the displayed factor
order.

Let $\mathcal N:A\to B$ be a finite-dimensional channel, let $V:A\to B\otimes E$ be a finite Stinespring isometry, let $\mathcal N^c(X)=\operatorname{Tr}_B(VXV^*)$, and let $\rho$ be a density operator on $A$. Then

$$I_c(\rho,\mathcal N)=S(\mathcal N(\rho))-S(\mathcal N^c(\rho)).$$

The right-hand side is independent of the chosen Stinespring dilation, since it equals the purification-defined quantity in [[def-it-quantum-channel-complement-and-coherent-information]].

derivations.claim: By [F1] and [F8], the coherent information of an input state is $(1-2\epsilon)S(\rho)$, with $S(\rho)\le\ln d$ and $S(\rho)\ge0$. If $\epsilon\le1/2$, its maximum is $(1-2\epsilon)\ln d$, attained at $I/d$.

Now suppose $\epsilon\ge1/2$. By [F2], there is an antidegrading channel $\mathcal A:E\to B$ with $\mathcal E=\mathcal A\circ\mathcal E^c$. Its tensor powers are channels by [F9]. For any $n$-use input state and purification reference $R$, [F5] gives $I(R;B^n)\le I(R;E^n)$. The joint state $RB^nE^n$ from a product Stinespring isometry is pure, so Schmidt decomposition gives $S(RB^n)=S(E^n)$ and $S(RE^n)=S(B^n)$. By the mutual-information definition [F6], $$I(R;B^n)-I(R;E^n)=S(B^n)-S(E^n)-S(RB^n)+S(RE^n)=2[S(B^n)-S(E^n)]=2I_c(\rho,\mathcal E^{\otimes n}),$$ where the last equality is [F10]. Hence the data-processing inequality forces $I_c(\rho,\mathcal E^{\otimes n})\le0$. A pure input attains zero, so the $n$-use coherent-information supremum is zero and [F4] gives $Q=0$.
For $\epsilon\le1/2$, [F2] says the channel is degradable; applying [F3] to step 1.1 gives $Q=P=(1-2\epsilon)\ln d$. This includes $\epsilon=1/2$, where the value is zero.

For any finite $n$-use ensemble, [F7] and [F6] express private information as $I(X;B^n)-I(X;E^n)$. The antidegrading channel on $E^n$ and [F5] make this difference nonpositive. The singleton ensemble has private information zero, so each $n$-use private-information supremum is zero; [F4] gives $P=0$.

By [F1] and [F4], the entanglement-assisted objective is $S(\rho)+I_c(\rho,\mathcal E_{d,\epsilon})=2(1-\epsilon)S(\rho)$. Since $2(1-\epsilon)\ge0$, [F8] makes its maximum $2(1-\epsilon)\ln d$, proving the final formula.

$$F_n:=\langle\Phi_{K_n}|(\operatorname{id}_{R_n}\otimes\mathcal D_n\mathcal N^{\otimes n}\mathcal W_n)(|\Phi_{K_n}\rangle\langle\Phi_{K_n}|)|\Phi_{K_n}\rangle,$$

where $\mathcal W_n(X)=W_nXW_n^*$. A rate is quantum-achievable if $F_n\to1$; the resulting capacity is $Q(\mathcal N)$. This is the subspace entanglement-transmission convention.

$$e_n^{EA}:=1-\frac1{K_n}\sum_{m=1}^{K_n}\operatorname{tr}\!\left[\Gamma_{m,n}\bigl((\mathcal N^{\otimes n}\circ\mathcal E_{m,n})\otimes\operatorname{id}_{S_B}\bigr)(\sigma_{S_AS_B})\right].$$ A rate is achievable when this error tends to zero; there is no constraint on the dimension or consumption of the shared entanglement. where $\psi_\rho$ is any finite purification of $\rho$ on $R\otimes A$. The value is additive: $C_E(\mathcal N_1\otimes\mathcal N_2)=C_E(\mathcal N_1)+C_E(\mathcal N_2)$ for finite-dimensional channels.

Let $A$ and $B$ be nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces and let $\mathcal N:\mathcal L(A)\to\mathcal L(B)$ be a quantum channel as in [[def-qc-quantum-channel]]. Choose a finite-dimensional environment $E$ and a linear isometry $V:A\to B\otimes E$ such that

$$\mathcal N(X)=\operatorname{Tr}_E(VXV^*)$$

for every $X\in\mathcal L(A)$; such a dilation exists by [[thm-qc-finite-stinespring-dilation]]. The channel

$$\mathcal N^c(X):=\operatorname{Tr}_B(VXV^*)\in\mathcal L(E)$$

is the **complementary channel associated with this chosen dilation**. The partial trace $\operatorname{Tr}_B$ contracts the first factor of the ordered product $B\otimes E$ ([[def-qc-first-factor-partial-trace]]).

It is a quantum channel: reorder $B\otimes E$ to $E\otimes B$ by the finite wire-permutation unitary ([[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]], [[thm-qc-wire-permutation-is-unitary]]); the reordered $V$ is still an isometry, so tracing its second factor $B$ gives a channel by [[thm-qc-isometry-partial-trace-is-channel]].

For a density operator $\rho$ on $A$, choose a finite purification $|\psi\rangle\in A\otimes R$ with $\operatorname{Tr}_R|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|=\rho$ ([[def-qc-ensemble-and-purification]]), and define $\omega_{BR}:=(\mathcal N\otimes\operatorname{id}_R)(|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|)$. Its **coherent information** from $A$ to $B$ is

$$I_c(\rho,\mathcal N):=S(\mathcal N(\rho))-S(\omega_{BR}),$$

where $S$ is finite-dimensional von Neumann entropy in nats ([[def-it-von-neumann-entropy]]). The value does not depend on the chosen purification: after padding reference spaces, any two purifications differ by a unitary on $R$ ([[thm-qc-purification-existence-and-unitary-equivalence]]); applying $\mathcal N\otimes\operatorname{id}_R$ preserves that unitary relation. A unitary maps an orthonormal eigenbasis to an orthonormal eigenbasis with the same eigenvalues, so entropy is unchanged ([[thm-complex-spectral-theorem-for-normal-endomorphisms]]). Padding adds only zero eigenvalues, which do not contribute.

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space of dimension $d$, and let $\rho$ be a density operator on $H$. Then

$$S(\rho)\le\ln d,$$

with equality if and only if $\rho=I_H/d$.

Let $Q_2=\mathbb C^2$ be the ordered qubit register with computational basis
$(|0\rangle,|1\rangle)$, and use the ordered two-factor register
$Q_2\otimes Q_2$ from [[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]]. Define the
four **Bell vectors** by

$$|\Phi^+\rangle:=\frac{|00\rangle+|11\rangle}{\sqrt2},\qquad |\Phi^-\rangle:=\frac{|00\rangle-|11\rangle}{\sqrt2},\qquad |\Psi^+\rangle:=\frac{|01\rangle+|10\rangle}{\sqrt2},\qquad |\Psi^-\rangle:=\frac{|01\rangle-|10\rangle}{\sqrt2}.$$

The ordered label convention is
$|00\rangle\mapsto|\Phi^+\rangle$,
$|01\rangle\mapsto|\Psi^+\rangle$,
$|10\rangle\mapsto|\Phi^-\rangle$, and
$|11\rangle\mapsto|\Psi^-\rangle$. Thus the first label is the phase/sign
bit and the second is the bit-flip bit. The next theorem verifies that these
vectors form an orthonormal basis and gives the corresponding preparation and
decoding maps.

For each input pair $(a,b)\in\{0,1\}^2$ in the procedure
[[alg-qc-dense-coding]], with $a$ the phase bit and $b$ the flip bit, Alice's
encoding $Z_A^aX_A^b$ sends $|\Phi^+\rangle$ to the Bell vector $B|ab\rangle$.
Bob's inverse $B^\dagger$ therefore returns the computational-basis vector
$|ab\rangle$, and the final projective measurement outputs the original two
bits with probability one. This realizes two classical output bits using one
preshared Bell pair and one transmitted qubit. It is an achievability result,
not an optimality claim.

derivations.claim: For any qubit input $\rho$, the identity channel leaves its purification $\psi_{RA}$ pure. Hence $S(RB)=0$ and $S(B)=S(\rho)$, so [F2] gives $I_c(\rho,\operatorname{id})=S(\rho)$. By [F1] and [F3], $C_E(\operatorname{id})=\max_\rho2S(\rho)=2\ln2$.

For the finite-dimensional flagged erasure channel $\mathcal E_{d,\epsilon}$ with input dimension $d\ge1$ and erasure probability $\epsilon\in[0,1]$,

$$Q(\mathcal E_{d,\epsilon})=P(\mathcal E_{d,\epsilon})=\max\{1-2\epsilon,0\}\ln d,\qquad C_E(\mathcal E_{d,\epsilon})=2(1-\epsilon)\ln d.$$

All capacities are in nats per channel use. The unassisted quantum and private formulas are zero in the antidegradable regime $\epsilon\ge1/2$.

For $\mathcal E_{d,\epsilon}$, choose the Stinespring isometry in [[thm-it-qudit-erasure-channel-is-cptp]], with environment $E=A\oplus\mathbb C e_E$. Its complement is

$$\mathcal E^c_{d,\epsilon}(X)=\epsilon J_EXJ_E^*\oplus(1-\epsilon)\operatorname{tr}(X)|e_E\rangle\langle e_E|.$$

The channel is degradable for $0\le\epsilon\le\tfrac12$ and antidegradable for $\tfrac12\le\epsilon\le1$.

Let $A$ be a $d$-dimensional complex inner-product space with $d\ge1$. Form the orthogonal direct sum $B:=A\oplus\mathbb C e$, where $e$ is a unit erasure vector orthogonal to every vector in $A$; the inner product on pairs is $\langle(x,a),(y,b)\rangle_B=\langle x,y\rangle_A+a\overline b$. Thus $\dim B=d+1$ by [[cor-dimension-of-a-direct-sum]]. Let $J:A\to B$ be the isometric inclusion into the data summand.

For an erasure probability $\epsilon\in[0,1]$, the **$d$-dimensional quantum erasure channel** is the linear map

$$\mathcal E_{d,\epsilon}(X):=(1-\epsilon)JXJ^*\oplus \epsilon\operatorname{tr}(X)|e\rangle\langle e|,\qquad X\in\mathcal L(A).$$

For a density operator $\rho$, this outputs the data state with probability $1-\epsilon$ and the orthogonal erasure flag with probability $\epsilon$. The definition is on the full operator space, and its channel property is established in [[thm-it-qudit-erasure-channel-is-cptp]].

Write $\ln$ for the natural logarithm $\log$ of [[def-natural-logarithm]]. Unless a base is displayed, every information quantity on this page uses $\ln$ and is measured in **nats**. For a base $b>1$ and $t>0$, define
$$\log_b t:=\frac{\ln t}{\ln b}.$$
The denominator is positive: $b>1$, $\ln$ is strictly increasing, and $\ln 1=0$ by [[thm-natural-logarithm-laws]]. A base-$b$ entropy or divergence is obtained by replacing each $\ln$ in the finite formulas below by $\log_b$; use $0\log_b0:=0$ and assign $+\infty$ to a positive numerator over a zero denominator. The case $b=2$ measures **bits**; $b=e$ gives nats.

derivations.claim: Substituting $d=2$ into [F1] and dividing by $\ln2$ gives $Q=P=\max\{1-2\epsilon,0\}$ bits and $C_E=2(1-\epsilon)$ bits. At $\epsilon=0,1/4,1/2,3/4,1$, these pairs are respectively $(1,2),(1/2,3/2),(0,1),(0,1/2),(0,0)$, which are the table entries.

By [F2], the first two probabilities lie in the degradable region, the last two lie in the antidegradable region, and the half-erasure point lies in both. At $\epsilon=1/2$, [F2] gives $\mathcal E^c(X)=\tfrac12J_EXJ_E^*\oplus\tfrac12\operatorname{tr}(X)|e_E\rangle\langle e_E|$, while [F3] gives $\mathcal E(X)=\tfrac12J_BXJ_B^*\oplus\tfrac12\operatorname{tr}(X)|e_B\rangle\langle e_B|$. The unitary identification $J_Bx\mapsto J_Ex$ and $e_B\mapsto e_E$ carries one map to the other, proving self-complementarity up to flag relabeling.

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, with the root convention that its inner product is linear in the first argument, and let $\rho$ be a density operator on $H$ ([[def-qc-density-operator]]). If $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_d$ are its eigenvalues counted with multiplicity, define its **von Neumann entropy** by

$$S(\rho):=-\operatorname{tr}(\rho\ln\rho):=-\sum_{j:\lambda_j>0}\lambda_j\ln\lambda_j.$$

The trace is the finite-dimensional endomorphism trace ([[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]), and the spectral definition makes the expression independent of the eigenbasis. The term for a zero eigenvalue is defined to be $0\ln0:=0$. The default unit is nats, using the natural logarithm ([[def-natural-logarithm]]); the entropy in bits is $S_2(\rho):=S(\rho)/\ln2$.

For density operators $\rho,\sigma$ on a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space,

$$D(\rho\|\sigma)\ge0,$$

with equality if and only if $\rho=\sigma$.

Let $H,K$ be finite-dimensional complex-inner-product spaces with the tensor-product convention of [[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]]. For every $\Psi\in H\otimes K$ there are an integer $r\ge0$, positive numbers $s_1,\ldots,s_r$, and orthonormal families $u_1,\ldots,u_r\in H$ and $v_1,\ldots,v_r\in K$ such that

$$\Psi=\sum_{j=1}^r s_j u_j\otimes v_j,\qquad \|\Psi\|^2=\sum_{j=1}^r s_j^2.$$

For $\Psi=0$ take $r=0$ and the empty sum. For any chosen ordered pair of orthonormal bases, the construction below obtains the $s_j$ as the positive singular values of the coefficient matrix of $\Psi$ in their ordered product basis.

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional vector space over $F$ and let $T:V\to V$ be
linear. Choose any ordered basis $\mathcal B$ of $V$ and define the **trace of
the endomorphism $T$** by

$$\operatorname{tr}(T):=\operatorname{tr}([T]_{\mathcal B}^{\mathcal B}).$$

This is independent of the chosen basis: matrices of the same endomorphism in
two ordered bases are similar, and similar matrices have equal trace. When
$V$ is the zero space, the empty basis gives trace $0$.

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional real or complex inner product space and let
$T:V\to V$ be linear. The following are equivalent:

1. $T$ is non-negative.
2. $T$ is self-adjoint and every eigenvalue of $T$ is a nonnegative real number.
3. Some orthonormal basis makes the matrix of $T$ diagonal with nonnegative real diagonal entries.
4. There exists a linear map $S:V\to V$ such that $T=S^*S$.

Let $H$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space and let $A,B:H\to H$ be non-negative operators. For such an operator $A$, set $\operatorname{supp}(A):=(\ker A)^\perp$, where $\ker A$ is the kernel of a linear map ([[def-kernel-and-image-of-a-linear-map]]); this extends the density-operator support convention in [[def-qc-density-operator]]. If $\operatorname{supp}(A)\subseteq\operatorname{supp}(B)$, define

$$D(A\|B):=\operatorname{tr}(A\ln A)-\operatorname{tr}(A\ln B).$$

Here $\ln A$ is defined spectrally on the positive eigenspaces of $A$ with $0\ln0:=0$, and $\ln B$ in the cross term is restricted to $\operatorname{supp}(B)$; the support condition ensures that $A$ vanishes on $\ker B$, so the omitted kernel contributes zero. If $\operatorname{supp}(A)\nsubseteq\operatorname{supp}(B)$, set $D(A\|B):=+\infty$. In particular, $D(0\|B)=0$. For density operators this is the finite-dimensional **quantum relative entropy**. The logarithms are natural, so the value is in nats; the base-two value is $D_2(A\|B):=D(A\|B)/\ln2$.

The function $\log:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ is continuous and strictly increasing, is onto $\mathbb R$, and satisfies, for $x,y>0$,
$$\log(xy)=\log x+\log y,\qquad \log(x/y)=\log x-\log y,\qquad \log(1/x)=-\log x.$$
Also $\log 1=0$.

derivations.claim: Omit zero weights. For each $i$ with $p_i>0$, $\bar\rho-p_i\rho_i=\sum_{j\ne i}p_j\rho_j$ is non-negative. If $v\in\ker\bar\rho$, its quadratic form under this sum is zero; every summand is nonnegative, so $\langle\rho_i v,v\rangle=0$ and [F5] gives $\rho_i v=0$. Hence $\operatorname{supp}\rho_i\subseteq\operatorname{supp}\bar\rho$ and every $D(\rho_i\|\bar\rho)$ is finite. The trace formula [F6], linearity of trace [F4], and $\bar\rho=\sum_i p_i\rho_i$ give $$\sum_i p_iD(\rho_i\Vert\bar\rho)=S(\bar\rho)-\sum_i p_iS(\rho_i)\ge0$$ by [F2].

For the upper bound, diagonalize each $\rho_i=\sum_j\lambda_{ij}|v_{ij}\rangle\langle v_{ij}|$, omitting zero weights and eigenvalues, and purify the mixture as $|v\rangle=\sum_{ij}\sqrt{p_i\lambda_{ij}}|v_{ij}\rangle\otimes|i,j\rangle$. Its label marginal $G$ is a state with diagonal $q_{ij}=p_i\lambda_{ij}$ and has the same nonzero eigenvalues as $\bar\rho$ by Schmidt decomposition. The logarithm product law in [F6] gives $H(q)=H(p)+\sum_i p_iS(\rho_i)$.

For $\Delta=\operatorname{diag}(q)$, its kernel is spanned by coordinate labels with $q_{ij}=0$. Each such basis vector $e_{ij}$ has $\langle Ge_{ij},e_{ij}\rangle=q_{ij}=0$, so [F5] gives $Ge_{ij}=0$. Hence $G$ annihilates $\ker\Delta$ and $\operatorname{supp}G\subseteq\operatorname{supp}\Delta$. The formula [F6] now gives $$0\le D(G\Vert\Delta)=H(q)-S(G)=H(p)+\sum_i p_iS(\rho_i)-S(\bar\rho).$$ This proves both bounds, including singleton/zero-weight cases.

Interchanging the states gives the absolute-value bound. Dimension one causes no exception. For $t>0$, [F7] gives $g'(t)=\ln(1+1/t)>0$ and $g''(t)=-1/[t(1+t)]<0$. Moreover $t\ln t\to0$ as $t\downarrow0$ by [F9], so $g$ is continuous on $[0,1]$ with the stated endpoint value. Jensen for $g$ follows from [F8] applied to the convex function $-g$, including the endpoint.

For each $m$, let $t_m=T(\sigma_m,\sigma)$. By step 1.1, $0\le t_m\le1$, so $a=M^{-1}\sum_m t_m\in[0,1]$. For states $\rho_i$ and finite probabilities $p_i$, put $\bar\rho=\sum_i p_i\rho_i$. Then
$$0\le S(\bar\rho)-\sum_i p_iS(\rho_i)\le H(p).$$

Let $A$ and $B$ be nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces and let $\mathcal N:\mathcal L(A)\to\mathcal L(B)$ be a quantum channel as in [[def-qc-quantum-channel]]. Choose a finite-dimensional environment $E$ and a linear isometry $V:A\to B\otimes E$ such that

$$\mathcal N(X)=\operatorname{Tr}_E(VXV^*)$$

for every $X\in\mathcal L(A)$; such a dilation exists by [[thm-qc-finite-stinespring-dilation]]. The channel

$$\mathcal N^c(X):=\operatorname{Tr}_B(VXV^*)\in\mathcal L(E)$$

is the **complementary channel associated with this chosen dilation**. The partial trace $\operatorname{Tr}_B$ contracts the first factor of the ordered product $B\otimes E$ ([[def-qc-first-factor-partial-trace]]).

It is a quantum channel: reorder $B\otimes E$ to $E\otimes B$ by the finite wire-permutation unitary ([[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]], [[thm-qc-wire-permutation-is-unitary]]); the reordered $V$ is still an isometry, so tracing its second factor $B$ gives a channel by [[thm-qc-isometry-partial-trace-is-channel]].

For a density operator $\rho$ on $A$, choose a finite purification $|\psi\rangle\in A\otimes R$ with $\operatorname{Tr}_R|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|=\rho$ ([[def-qc-ensemble-and-purification]]), and define $\omega_{BR}:=(\mathcal N\otimes\operatorname{id}_R)(|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|)$. Its **coherent information** from $A$ to $B$ is

$$I_c(\rho,\mathcal N):=S(\mathcal N(\rho))-S(\omega_{BR}),$$

where $S$ is finite-dimensional von Neumann entropy in nats ([[def-it-von-neumann-entropy]]). The value does not depend on the chosen purification: after padding reference spaces, any two purifications differ by a unitary on $R$ ([[thm-qc-purification-existence-and-unitary-equivalence]]); applying $\mathcal N\otimes\operatorname{id}_R$ preserves that unitary relation. A unitary maps an orthonormal eigenbasis to an orthonormal eigenbasis with the same eigenvalues, so entropy is unchanged ([[thm-complex-spectral-theorem-for-normal-endomorphisms]]). Padding adds only zero eigenvalues, which do not contribute.

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner product space and let $T:V\to V$
be linear. Then $T$ is normal if and only if $V$ has an orthonormal basis
consisting of eigenvectors of $T$.

Let $\mathcal N:A\to B$ be a finite-dimensional channel, let $V:A\to B\otimes E$ be a finite Stinespring isometry, let $\mathcal N^c(X)=\operatorname{Tr}_B(VXV^*)$, and let $\rho$ be a density operator on $A$. Then

$$I_c(\rho,\mathcal N)=S(\mathcal N(\rho))-S(\mathcal N^c(\rho)).$$

The right-hand side is independent of the chosen Stinespring dilation, since it equals the purification-defined quantity in [[def-it-quantum-channel-complement-and-coherent-information]].

$$\log(xy)=\log x+\log y,\qquad \log(x/y)=\log x-\log y,\qquad \log(1/x)=-\log x.$$
Also $\log 1=0$.

For a finite nonempty set identified with $[k]=\{1,\ldots,k\}$, a **probability vector** is $p=(p_i)_{i=1}^k$ with $p_i\ge0$ and $\sum_i p_i=1$; it is the outcome-weight vector of a finite probability space ([[def-finite-probability-space-and-event]]). Its Shannon entropy in natural units is
$$H(p):=-\sum_{i=1}^k p_i\ln p_i,$$
with $0\ln0:=0$. For probability vectors $p,q$ on the same set $[k]$, the relative entropy is
$$D(p\|q):=\sum_{i:p_i>0}p_i\ln(p_i/q_i),$$
with value $+\infty$ if $p_i>0=q_i$ for some $i$. A matrix $A\in[0,1]^{N\times m}$ is **row-stochastic** when each row sums to one. For a probability row vector $p$ on $[m]$ and a row vector $X\in[0,1]^m$, the dot product $pX^{\mathsf T}=\sum_{i=1}^m p_iX_i$ is the acceptance probability under distribution $p$.

These definitions use finite sets only; entropy is between $0$ and $\ln k$, as proved where needed below.

For probability vectors $p=(p_i)_{i\in I}$ and $q=(q_i)_{i\in I}$ on a finite nonempty set $I$, define

$$D(p\|q):=\begin{cases}\displaystyle\sum_{i:p_i>0}p_i\ln\frac{p_i}{q_i},&p_i>0\Rightarrow q_i>0,\\+\infty,&\text{otherwise.}\end{cases}$$

Then $D(p\|q)\ge0$, and $D(p\|q)=0$ if and only if $p=q$.

Let $P_t$ project onto the span of the words of type $t$ and set $\tau_t=P_t/m_t$. These states are flat, their supports are mutually orthogonal, and $$\rho^{\otimes n}=\sum_{t:p_t>0}p_t\tau_t.$$ There are at most $(n+1)^d$ types. If $N_T$ is their number and $u$ is the uniform law on them, [F6] gives $0\le D(p\|u)=\ln N_T-H(T)$, so $H(T)\le d\ln(n+1)$. Since $S(\tau_t)=\ln m_t$, the logarithm product law [F5] and $\sum_t p_t n_j=n\lambda_j$ yield $$\sum_t p_tS(\tau_t)=\sum_t p_t\ln m_t=nS(\rho)-H(T).$$

Let $B_t=\mathcal N^{\otimes n}(\tau_t)$ and $E_t=(\mathcal N^c)^{\otimes n}(\tau_t)$, with averages $\bar B=\sum_tp_tB_t=\mathcal N(\rho)^{\otimes n}$ and $\bar E=\sum_tp_tE_t=\mathcal N^c(\rho)^{\otimes n}$. By [F4], the receiver-minus-environment entropy identity applies to each type. The lower mixture bound [F1] gives $\sum_tp_tS(B_t)\ge S(\bar B)-H(T)$, while its upper bound gives $\sum_tp_tS(E_t)\le S(\bar E)$. Product spectral decompositions and [F5] give $S(\bar B)-S(\bar E)=n[S(\mathcal N(\rho))-S(\mathcal N^c(\rho))]=nI_c(\rho,\mathcal N)$. Hence $$\sum_tp_t I_c(\tau_t,\mathcal N^{\otimes n})\ge nI_c(\rho,\mathcal N)-H(T).$$ Adding $\sum_tp_tS(\tau_t)=nS(\rho)-H(T)$ from step 1.1 gives the second inequality.

Each displayed left side in step 2.1 is an average over the finite positive-probability types, so at least one type attains at least the corresponding average lower bound. These are exact finite-$n$ estimates; no replacement of fixed-dimensional continuity by a uniform bound is involved.

be linear. Then $T$ is normal if and only if $V$ has an orthonormal basis
consisting of eigenvectors of $T$.

Let $A:H\to K$ be a linear map ([[def-linear-map]]) between finite-dimensional complex
inner-product spaces. Then

$$\|A\|_1=\max\{\,|\operatorname{tr}_H(B^*A)|: B:H\to K\text{ linear and }\|B\|\le1\,\}.$$

Consequently, on the vector space of linear maps $H\to K$, the trace norm is
nonnegative, absolutely homogeneous, definite, and satisfies the triangle
inequality.

For vectors $u,v$ in a real or complex inner product space,

$$|\langle u,v\rangle|\le\lVert u\rVert\lVert v\rVert.$$

Equality holds if and only if $u$ and $v$ are linearly dependent, including the case in which either vector is zero.

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional vector space over $F$ and let $T:V\to V$ be
linear. Choose any ordered basis $\mathcal B$ of $V$ and define the **trace of
the endomorphism $T$** by

$$\operatorname{tr}(T):=\operatorname{tr}([T]_{\mathcal B}^{\mathcal B}).$$

This is independent of the chosen basis: matrices of the same endomorphism in
two ordered bases are similar, and similar matrices have equal trace. When
$V$ is the zero space, the empty basis gives trace $0$.

An **ordered tensor register** consists of a finite ordered list of
finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces $H_0,\ldots,H_{n-1}$, each
equipped with a specified ordered orthonormal basis. Its space is
$H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1}$, with factors retained in the displayed
order. The product basis is ordered lexicographically by its tuple of factor
indices. The empty tensor product is $\mathbb C$ with basis $\{1\}$. A
zero-dimensional factor is allowed in this mathematical construction and makes
the tensor space zero; it is not a register under
[[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]].

The inner product is linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the
second, and on elementary tensors it is

$$\left\langle\bigotimes_{k<n}x_k,\bigotimes_{k<n}y_k\right\rangle_{\otimes}:=\prod_{k<n}\langle x_k,y_k\rangle_{{\rm root},k}.$$ 

For the empty tensor, the right side is the empty product $1$, giving the
standard inner product on $\mathbb C$.

For a permutation $\sigma$ of the $n$ factor positions, the **wire permutation**
$P_\sigma$ maps the product basis vector indexed by
$(i_0,\ldots,i_{n-1})$ to the product basis vector whose output factor order is
$(\sigma(0),\ldots,\sigma(n-1))$. It is extended linearly; for $n=0$ it is the
identity on $\mathbb C$. The extension is a linear map in the sense of
[[def-linear-map]].

1. $T$ is non-negative.
2. $T$ is self-adjoint and every eigenvalue of $T$ is a nonnegative real number.
3. Some orthonormal basis makes the matrix of $T$ diagonal with nonnegative real diagonal entries.
4. There exists a linear map $S:V\to V$ such that $T=S^*S$.

$$\|P\|_1=\operatorname{tr}_H(P).$$

$\langle Pv,v\rangle\ge0$ for all $v$, as in
[[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]].

Let $R$ be the real rotation by $\pi/4$ in coordinates 1 and 2, acting identically elsewhere. Use the symmetric finite list $\mathcal S=G\cup\{R,R^*\}$, retaining multiplicities if any. At each walk step choose the identity with probability $1/2$ and an element of this list uniformly with the remaining probability. Moreover $$\langle X,(I-T_j)X\rangle=\frac1{4|\mathcal S|}\sum_{U\in\mathcal S}\|X-U^{\otimes j}X(U^*)^{\otimes j}\|_2^2.$$ Thus their fixed spaces are exactly the simultaneous commutants of the displayed finite unitaries.

For $j=1$, the independent diagonal fifth-root phases force a commuting matrix to be diagonal; permutations force all its diagonal entries equal. For $j=2$, a matrix coefficient from $|i,j\rangle$ to $|k,l\rangle$ can survive the diagonal phases only when the unordered multisets $\{i,j\}$ and $\{k,l\}$ agree. By the primitive-order identity established in step 1.1, each index occurs with multiplicity 0, 1 or 2; equality modulo 5 of every exponent forces equality of these integer multiplicities. Commutation with all permutations then leaves three constants: $c$ on $|i,i\rangle$, $a$ on $|i,j\rangle\langle i,j|$ for $i\ne j$, and $b$ on $|i,j\rangle\langle j,i|$. Commutation with $R\otimes R$ applied to $|1,1\rangle$, whose rotated vector has nonzero coefficients on both $|1,2\rangle$ and $|2,1\rangle$, forces $c=a+b$. Conversely $I$ and the swap $F$ commute with every tensor-square unitary. The fixed space is therefore precisely $\operatorname{span}\{I,F\}$, also when $D=2$.

Finite-dimensional spectral decomposition now gives orthogonal projections $\mathcal P_1,\mathcal P_2$ onto these fixed spaces and a number $0\le\lambda<1$ such that $$\|T_j^L-\mathcal P_j\|_{2\to2}\le\lambda^L,\qquad j=1,2.$$ If the orthogonal complement is zero, take its spectral radius as zero. Every $T_j^L$ is the moment of an finite distribution of length-$L$ unitary words; the limit is only a finite-matrix spectral calculation, not an assumed Haar integral. The first projection is $\mathcal P_1(X)=\operatorname{tr}(X)I/D$. For any rank-$K$ projection $P_0$, invariance of trace and swap trace gives $$\mathcal P_2(P_0\otimes P_0)=a_0I+b_0F,\qquad a_0=\frac{K(KD-1)}{D(D^2-1)},\quad b_0=\frac{K(D-K)}{D(D^2-1)}.$$ The coefficients solve $a_0D^2+b_0D=K^2$ and $a_0D+b_0D^2=K$.

Choose a coordinate isometry $W_0$ and let $W=UW_0$, where $U$ is a finite walk word. Complex conjugation preserves the same limiting first and second moment projections and their norm bounds, so they apply to $P=\overline W W^T$ as well. The swap identity on matrix units gives the following limiting second moment, with $\Omega=I_R/K\otimes\omega_E$: $$\lim_{L\to\infty}\mathbb E\|\omega^W-\Omega\|_2^2 =\frac{D(KD-1)}{K(D^2-1)}\operatorname{tr}(\omega^2)+\frac{1-DK}{K(D^2-1)}\operatorname{tr}(\omega_E^2) \le2\operatorname{tr}(\omega^2).$$ In detail, the squared-state term is $(D^2/K^2)\{a_0\operatorname{tr}(\omega^2)+b_0\operatorname{tr}(\omega_E^2)\}$, and the limiting mean is $\Omega$, so subtract $\operatorname{tr}(\omega_E^2)/K$.

The finite moment error has a quantitative bound. Put $d_E=\dim E$ and $\varepsilon=\lambda^L$. The first-moment error in each matrix unit of the compressed reference is at most $\varepsilon$ in Hilbert–Schmidt norm; contracting it with $\omega$ shows $\|\mathbb E\omega^W-\Omega\|_2\le D\varepsilon\|\omega\|_2\le D\varepsilon$. For the squared-state term, the second-moment error on $P_0\otimes P_0$ has Hilbert–Schmidt norm at most $K\varepsilon$. In its trace pairing with $F_E(\omega\otimes\omega)$, the partial trace over the two environment copies has Hilbert–Schmidt norm at most $d_E\|\omega\|_2^2\le d_E$ (Cauchy–Schwarz for each diagonal block). Consequently that squared-state error is at most $D^2d_E\varepsilon/K$. The cross term with $\Omega$, whose Hilbert–Schmidt norm is at most $1/\sqrt K$, has error at most $2D\varepsilon/\sqrt K$. Hence, with $C_D=D^2d_E+2D$, $$\mathbb E\|\omega^W-\Omega\|_2^2\le2\operatorname{tr}(\omega^2)+C_D\varepsilon.$$ Positivity implies $\operatorname{supp}\omega\subseteq A\otimes\operatorname{supp}\omega_E$: if $v\in\ker\omega_E$, the marginal quadratic form is a sum of nonnegative diagonal quadratic forms of $\omega$; each is zero, and [F6] makes the corresponding product vectors kernel vectors of $\omega$. Self-adjointness then makes the corresponding rows and columns zero. Compression acts only on $A$, so both $\omega^W$ and $\Omega$ are supported in $\mathbb C^K\otimes\operatorname{supp}\omega_E$; each difference therefore has rank at most $Kr$. Cauchy–Schwarz on singular values and Jensen give the trace-norm bound at most $\sqrt{2Kr\operatorname{tr}(\omega^2)}+\sqrt{KrC_D\varepsilon}$.

Finally write a Hermitian $Z$ as $Z_+-Z_-$ using [F8]. Each compression of $Z_+$ or $Z_-$ is positive, so its trace norm is its trace by [F7]; positivity and linearity therefore bound the trace norm of the difference by the sum of the two compressed traces. The first-moment bound $\|\mathbb EP-(K/D)I\|_\infty\le\sqrt K\varepsilon$ gives $$\mathbb E\|\mathcal C_W(Z)\|_1\le(1+D\varepsilon/\sqrt K)\|Z\|_1.$$ Choose a finite $L$ with both $KrC_D\lambda^L\le\delta^2$ and $D\lambda^L/\sqrt K\le\delta$. Such an integer exists by $\lambda<1$; the least such integer is a specified choice. If $r=0$, the positive operator is zero and its decoupling bound is automatic. This proves both assertions with an finite ensemble and exact dimension-dependent moment control.

Let $D\ge2$, $1\le K\le D$, and $\omega_{AE}\succeq0$ with $\dim A=D$, $\operatorname{tr}\omega\le1$, and $r=\operatorname{rank}\omega_E$. For every $\delta>0$ there is an explicitly specified finite probability ensemble of isometries $W:\mathbb C^K\to\mathbb C^D$ such that, for
$$\omega^W_{RE}=\frac DK(W^T\otimes I_E)\omega_{AE}(\overline W\otimes I_E),$$
one has
$$\mathbb E\left\|\omega^W_{RE}-\frac{I_R}{K}\otimes\omega_E\right\|_1\le\sqrt{2Kr\operatorname{tr}(\omega_{AE}^2)}+\delta.$$
At the same time the ensemble can be required to satisfy, for every Hermitian $Z_{AE}$,
$$\mathbb E\left\|\frac DK(W^T\otimes I)Z(\overline W\otimes I)\right\|_1\le(1+\delta)\|Z\|_1.$$
No Haar existence or Gaussian-law supplier, and no choice axiom, is used.

For every fixed finite ensemble $p_x,\rho_x$ and fixed $\eta>0$, there are constants $C,c>0$ (depending on this ensemble and $\eta$, not $n$) and projectors $P_n,Q_{x^n}$ such that, writing $\bar\rho=\sum p_x\rho_x$ and $s=\sum p_xS(\rho_x)$,
$$\operatorname{rank}P_n\le e^{n(S(\bar\rho)+\eta)},\quad P_n\bar\rho^{\otimes n}P_n\preceq e^{-n(S(\bar\rho)-\eta)}P_n,$$
$$\operatorname{rank}Q_{x^n}\le e^{n(s+\eta)},\quad Q_{x^n}\rho_{x^n}Q_{x^n}\preceq e^{-n(s-\eta)}Q_{x^n},$$
and
$$\mathbb E\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{X^n}(I-P_n))\le Ce^{-cn},\qquad\mathbb E\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{X^n}(I-Q_{X^n}))\le Ce^{-cn}.$$
The second pair of algebraic bounds holds for every word, including words with zero sampling probability; no per-word high-acceptance assertion is required.

Let $\rho$ be a density operator on a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space $H$, let $0\preceq\Lambda\preceq I_H$, and suppose $\operatorname{tr}(\Lambda\rho)\ge1-u$ for some $u\in[0,1]$. Then

$$\left\|\rho-\sqrt{\Lambda}\rho\sqrt{\Lambda}\right\|_1\le2\sqrt{u}.$$

Here $\sqrt{\Lambda}$ is the unique nonnegative square root, and $\|\cdot\|_1$ is the finite-dimensional trace norm. No normalization is applied after the operation $\rho\mapsto\sqrt{\Lambda}\rho\sqrt{\Lambda}$.

Let $H,K$ be finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces and let
$\Phi:\mathcal L(H)\to\mathcal L(K)$ be a quantum channel. It has a finite
Kraus representation, and for any chosen such representation with $N$
operators $K_a:H\to K$ there are an $N$-dimensional environment $E$ and a
linear isometry $V:H\to K\otimes E$ such that
$$\Phi(X)=\operatorname{Tr}_E(VXV^\dagger)\quad\text{for every }X\in\mathcal L(H).$$

Let $H,K$ be finite-dimensional complex-inner-product spaces with the tensor-product convention of [[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]]. For every $\Psi\in H\otimes K$ there are an integer $r\ge0$, positive numbers $s_1,\ldots,s_r$, and orthonormal families $u_1,\ldots,u_r\in H$ and $v_1,\ldots,v_r\in K$ such that

$$\Psi=\sum_{j=1}^r s_j u_j\otimes v_j,\qquad \|\Psi\|^2=\sum_{j=1}^r s_j^2.$$

For $\Psi=0$ take $r=0$ and the empty sum. For any chosen ordered pair of orthonormal bases, the construction below obtains the $s_j$ as the positive singular values of the coefficient matrix of $\Psi$ in their ordered product basis.

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space and let $\rho,\sigma\in\mathcal D(H)$. For every auxiliary space $R$ with $\dim R\ge\dim H$, a **purification** of $\rho$ on $H\otimes R$ means a unit vector $x$ with $\operatorname{Tr}_R(|x\rangle\langle x|)=\rho$. Then
$$F(\rho,\sigma)=\max\{|\langle x,y\rangle|:x,y\in H\otimes R,\ \|x\|=\|y\|=1,\ \operatorname{Tr}_R|x\rangle\langle x|=\rho,\ \operatorname{Tr}_R|y\rangle\langle y|=\sigma\}.$$
In particular, the maximum is attained with $R\cong H$.

Every density operator $\rho$ on a nonzero finite-dimensional complex-inner-product space $H$ has a purification on some finite-dimensional auxiliary space. More precisely, if $r=\operatorname{rank}(\rho)$, it has one on an auxiliary space of dimension $r$. If $\Psi_i\in H\otimes K_i$ ($i=1,2$) are any two purifications of the same $\rho$, then for every integer $m\ge\max(\dim K_1,\dim K_2)$ and every pair of linear isometric embeddings $\iota_i:K_i\to\mathbb C^m$, where $\mathbb C^m$ has its standard complex inner product, there is a unitary $U$ on $\mathbb C^m$ such that

$$ (I_H\otimes U)(I_H\otimes\iota_2)\Psi_2=(I_H\otimes\iota_1)\Psi_1. $$

For density operators $\rho,\sigma$ on a nonzero finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space,
$$1-F(\rho,\sigma)\le D(\rho,\sigma)\le\sqrt{1-F(\rho,\sigma)^2},$$
where $F$ is root fidelity and $D(\rho,\sigma)=\tfrac12\|\rho-\sigma\|_1$.

Let $H_A,H_E$ be finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces and let $X=X^\dagger$ be an endomorphism of $H_A\otimes H_E$. Then
$$\|\operatorname{Tr}_E X\|_1\le\|X\|_1.$$
The trace norm and partial trace are those of [[def-qc-trace-norm]] and [[def-qc-partial-trace]]. If either factor is zero-dimensional, both sides are zero.

Let $H_A,H_B,H_C$ be nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces and let $\rho_{ABC}$ be a density operator on their ordered tensor product. Write $\rho_{AB},\rho_{BC},\rho_B$ for its marginals using the partial traces in [[def-qc-partial-trace]]. Then
$$S(\rho_{AB})+S(\rho_{BC})\ge S(\rho_B)+S(\rho_{ABC}),$$
where $S(\rho)=-\operatorname{tr}(\rho\ln\rho)$ with $0\ln0:=0$ as in [[def-it-von-neumann-entropy]].

Let $A$ and $B$ be nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces and let $\mathcal N:\mathcal L(A)\to\mathcal L(B)$ be a quantum channel as in [[def-qc-quantum-channel]]. Choose a finite-dimensional environment $E$ and a linear isometry $V:A\to B\otimes E$ such that

$$\mathcal N(X)=\operatorname{Tr}_E(VXV^*)$$

for every $X\in\mathcal L(A)$; such a dilation exists by [[thm-qc-finite-stinespring-dilation]]. The channel

$$\mathcal N^c(X):=\operatorname{Tr}_B(VXV^*)\in\mathcal L(E)$$

is the **complementary channel associated with this chosen dilation**. The partial trace $\operatorname{Tr}_B$ contracts the first factor of the ordered product $B\otimes E$ ([[def-qc-first-factor-partial-trace]]).

It is a quantum channel: reorder $B\otimes E$ to $E\otimes B$ by the finite wire-permutation unitary ([[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]], [[thm-qc-wire-permutation-is-unitary]]); the reordered $V$ is still an isometry, so tracing its second factor $B$ gives a channel by [[thm-qc-isometry-partial-trace-is-channel]].

For a density operator $\rho$ on $A$, choose a finite purification $|\psi\rangle\in A\otimes R$ with $\operatorname{Tr}_R|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|=\rho$ ([[def-qc-ensemble-and-purification]]), and define $\omega_{BR}:=(\mathcal N\otimes\operatorname{id}_R)(|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|)$. Its **coherent information** from $A$ to $B$ is

$$I_c(\rho,\mathcal N):=S(\mathcal N(\rho))-S(\omega_{BR}),$$

where $S$ is finite-dimensional von Neumann entropy in nats ([[def-it-von-neumann-entropy]]). The value does not depend on the chosen purification: after padding reference spaces, any two purifications differ by a unitary on $R$ ([[thm-qc-purification-existence-and-unitary-equivalence]]); applying $\mathcal N\otimes\operatorname{id}_R$ preserves that unitary relation. A unitary maps an orthonormal eigenbasis to an orthonormal eigenbasis with the same eigenvalues, so entropy is unchanged ([[thm-complex-spectral-theorem-for-normal-endomorphisms]]). Padding adds only zero eigenvalues, which do not contribute.

Let $\mathcal N:A\to B$ be a finite-dimensional channel, let $V:A\to B\otimes E$ be a finite Stinespring isometry, let $\mathcal N^c(X)=\operatorname{Tr}_B(VXV^*)$, and let $\rho$ be a density operator on $A$. Then

$$I_c(\rho,\mathcal N)=S(\mathcal N(\rho))-S(\mathcal N^c(\rho)).$$

The right-hand side is independent of the chosen Stinespring dilation, since it equals the purification-defined quantity in [[def-it-quantum-channel-complement-and-coherent-information]].

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space of dimension $d$, and let $\rho$ be a density operator on $H$. Then

$$S(\rho)\le\ln d,$$

with equality if and only if $\rho=I_H/d$.

The function $\log:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ is continuous and strictly increasing, is onto $\mathbb R$, and satisfies, for $x,y>0$,
$$\log(xy)=\log x+\log y,\qquad \log(x/y)=\log x-\log y,\qquad \log(1/x)=-\log x.$$
Also $\log 1=0$.

Let $H,K,E$ be finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces and let
$V:H\to K\otimes E$ be a linear isometry. Then
$$\Phi(X)=\operatorname{Tr}_E(VXV^\dagger),\qquad X\in\mathcal L(H),$$
is a quantum channel from $H$ to $K$.

derivations.claim: Put $s_B=S(\mathcal N(\tau))$ and $s_E=S(\mathcal N^c(\tau))$. By [F11], $s_B-s_E=I_c(\tau,\mathcal N)$; choose $\eta>0$ with $R<s_B-s_E-2\eta$. On $n$ uses, let $|v_n\rangle=(I\otimes V^{\otimes n})|\Phi_{d^n}\rangle$ in factor order $A'B^nE^n$. Let $P_n,Q_n$ be the spectral projectors for the IID receiver and environment states from [[lem-it-exponential-cq-spectral-projectors]], and let $\epsilon_n\le Ce^{-cn}$ bound the sum of their failure probabilities. The commuting joint projection has acceptance at least $1-\epsilon_n$. For $$|\widehat v_n\rangle=(I_{A'}\otimes P_n\otimes Q_n)|v_n\rangle,$$ the rank-two pure-vector calculation used in gentle measurement gives $$\bigl\||v_n\rangle\langle v_n|-|\widehat v_n\rangle\langle\widehat v_n|\bigr\|_1\le2\sqrt{\epsilon_n}.$$ This follows also by applying the gentle-measurement lemma to the pure state and the joint projection. Let $\omega=\operatorname{Tr}_{B^n}|\widehat v_n\rangle\langle\widehat v_n|$. Its environment rank is at most $e^{n(s_E+\eta)}$. Since the projected vector is pure, $$\operatorname{tr}(\omega^2)=\operatorname{tr}(\omega_{B^n}^2).$$ Moreover $$0\preceq\omega_{B^n}\preceq P_n\mathcal N(\tau)^{\otimes n}P_n\preceq e^{-n(s_B-\eta)}P_n.$$ To verify the first inequality, take the partial trace after $Q_n$; the complementary environment projection produces another positive summand of the original receiver marginal. Hence $\operatorname{tr}(\omega^2)\le e^{-n(s_B-\eta)}$, because its trace is at most one.

First prove $s_B\le\ln d+s_E$. The one-use Stinespring output of $|\Phi_d\rangle$ is pure on $A'BE$, so [F5] gives $s_B=S(A'E)$. For its marginal state $\omega_{A'E}$, append a one-dimensional register $C$ in a pure state and order the resulting state as $A'CE$. Strong subadditivity [F10] gives $S(A'C)+S(CE)\ge S(C)+S(A'CE)$, that is $S(A')+S(E)\ge S(A'E)$; [F12] gives $S(A')=\ln d$. Hence $s_B\le\ln d+s_E$, so $I_c=s_B-s_E\le\ln d$ and $0<R<I_c$ implies $K_n=\lfloor e^{nR}\rfloor\le d^n$ by [F12]. For an isometry $W:\mathbb C^{K_n}\to A^{\otimes n}$, let $\rho^W_{RE^n}$ be the environment/reference state produced by encoding half of $|\Phi_{K_n}\rangle$. Coefficient matrices give exactly the normalized-compression expression for the unprojected marginal. Use the finite ensemble above with tolerance $e^{-n}$. Apply its compression estimate to $\omega$, and its averaged trace-contraction estimate to the difference between projected and unprojected marginals. Their environment marginals differ by at most $2\sqrt{\epsilon_n}$. The triangle inequality therefore yields $$\mathbb E\left\|\rho^W_{RE^n}-\frac{I_R}{K_n}\otimes\mathcal N^c(\tau)^{\otimes n}\right\|_1 \le6\sqrt{\epsilon_n}+2e^{-n}+\sqrt{2e^{-n(s_B-s_E-R-2\eta)}}\longrightarrow0.$$ Order the finite generator list and its length-$L$ words. For each $n$, take the first word whose displayed norm is at most twice its expectation; if that expectation is zero, take the first zero-norm word. A qualifying word exists by finite averaging. This specifies the entire encoder sequence without countable choices.

The product target is purified by $|\Phi_{K_n}\rangle_{RM}\otimes|e_n\rangle_{E^nF}$, with a sufficiently large finite $F$. The encoded Stinespring output is another purification on reference/environment versus receiver. Root-fidelity purification characterization, after adding a pure finite ancilla to the receiver if needed, supplies an isometry on the receiver's purifying space whose overlap with that target is the root fidelity of the two marginals. The fixed-purification form follows from the purification/unitary-equivalence theorem. Fuchs–van de Graaf makes this root fidelity at least one minus half the displayed norm. Trace out the extra decoder factor $F$: the resulting CPTP decoder has squared entanglement fidelity at least the square of that overlap and hence tending to one. The encoder is exactly the isometry $W$; no generating-code/transmitting-code equivalence is assumed. Fix ordered bases throughout. In the purification characterization use the polar/SVD attaining map, extending every kernel partial isometry by the ordered basis completion; in repeated eigenspaces, project the ordered coordinate vectors and Gram–Schmidt in that order. This specifies a decoder at each block length by one formula, rather than choosing a sequence of unrelated attaining maps.

If $I_c(\tau,\mathcal N)\le0$, choose a unit vector of $A^{\otimes n}$ as the encoder for $K_n=1$. The decoder to $\mathbb C$ is $X\mapsto\operatorname{tr}(X)$, a channel by [F13] using the isometry $x\mapsto1\otimes x$ and tracing $A^{\otimes n}$. Its entanglement fidelity is one and its rate is zero. For a subspace inclusion $J:\mathbb C^D\to A$, the restricted channel $\mathcal N_J(X)=\mathcal N(JXJ^*)$ has dilation $VJ$, and its flat input $I_D/D$ has coherent information $I_c(JJ^*/D,\mathcal N)$ by the fixed-dilation definition. Applying steps 1.1–3.1 to $\mathcal N_J$ and composing each encoder with $J^{\otimes n}$ proves the stated subspace case.
