$$\operatorname{rank}Q_{x^n}\le e^{n(s+\eta)},\quad Q_{x^n}\rho_{x^n}Q_{x^n}\preceq e^{-n(s-\eta)}Q_{x^n},$$
and
$$\mathbb E\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{X^n}(I-P_n))\le Ce^{-cn},\qquad\mathbb E\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{X^n}(I-Q_{X^n}))\le Ce^{-cn}.$$
The second pair of algebraic bounds holds for every word, including words with zero sampling probability; no per-word high-acceptance assertion is required.

Write $h(t)=-t\ln t-(1-t)\ln(1-t)$ with continuous endpoints. Let $g(t)=(1+t)\ln(1+t)-t\ln t$ for $t\in[0,1]$, with $g(0)=0$. For states $\rho,\sigma$ on dimension $d\ge1$ and $t=\frac12\|\rho-\sigma\|_1$, $$|S(\rho)-S(\sigma)|\le t\ln d+g(t).$$ Moreover, if $\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_M$ are states on that space and $a=M^{-1}\sum_m\frac12\|\sigma_m-\sigma\|_1$, their uniform Holevo information is at most $2a\ln d+2g(a)$. In particular on dimension $d_E^n$, exponential decay of $a$ makes unnormalized Holevo information tend to zero.

Let $\rho$ be a density operator on a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space $H$, let $0\preceq\Lambda\preceq I_H$, and suppose $\operatorname{tr}(\Lambda\rho)\ge1-u$ for some $u\in[0,1]$. Then

$$\left\|\rho-\sqrt{\Lambda}\rho\sqrt{\Lambda}\right\|_1\le2\sqrt{u}.$$

Here $\sqrt{\Lambda}$ is the unique nonnegative square root, and $\|\cdot\|_1$ is the finite-dimensional trace norm. No normalization is applied after the operation $\rho\mapsto\sqrt{\Lambda}\rho\sqrt{\Lambda}$.

Let $S,T$ be nonnegative endomorphisms of a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space $H$, with $S\preceq I_H$. Define $(S+T)^{-1/2}$ spectrally on $\operatorname{supp}(S+T)$ and set it to zero on $\ker(S+T)$. Then

$$I_H-(S+T)^{-1/2}S(S+T)^{-1/2}\preceq2(I_H-S)+4T.$$

Let $X$ be a finite nonempty classical label set, represented by a register $H_X$ with computational orthonormal basis $(\xi_x)_{x\in X}$ ([[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]]). For each $x$, write $\Pi_xz:=\langle z,\xi_x\rangle\xi_x$, the rank-one orthogonal projection using the root linear-first convention, as in [[lem-it-finite-cq-block-sum-is-a-state]]. Let $H_B$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space. A finite **classical-quantum state** is

$$\rho_{XB}:=\sum_{x\in X}p_x\Pi_x\otimes\rho_x,$$

where $p_x\ge0$, $\sum_xp_x=1$, and each $\rho_x$ is a density operator on $H_B$. It is a density operator by [[lem-it-finite-cq-block-sum-is-a-state]]. Its quantum marginal is $\bar\rho_B:=\sum_xp_x\rho_x=\operatorname{Tr}_X\rho_{XB}$ by the second-factor partial-trace formula in [[def-qc-partial-trace]], and it is a density operator by [[lem-it-partial-traces-of-a-state-are-states]]. The **Holevo information** of this ensemble is

$$\chi(\{p_x,\rho_x\}_{x\in X}):=S(\bar\rho_B)-\sum_{x:p_x>0}p_xS(\rho_x),$$

where zero-probability branches contribute nothing. This is measured in nats under [[def-it-von-neumann-entropy]].

Let $H$ and $K$ be finite-dimensional (have finite bases by [[def-dimension]])
complex inner-product spaces. A
**quantum channel** from $H$ to $K$ is a complex-linear map
$\Phi:\mathcal L(H)\to\mathcal L(K)$ ([[def-linear-map]]) that is completely
positive ([[def-qc-completely-positive-map]]) and trace-preserving, meaning

$$\operatorname{tr}(\Phi(X))=\operatorname{tr}(X)\qquad\text{for every }X\in\mathcal L(H),$$

where trace is the basis-independent trace of a finite-dimensional
endomorphism ([[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]). Trace preservation is
required on the full operator space, not only on density operators. This
definition is mathematical and assumes no physical realization.

Let $A:H\to K$ be a linear map ([[def-linear-map]]) between finite-dimensional complex
inner-product spaces. Then

$$\|A\|_1=\max\{\,|\operatorname{tr}_H(B^*A)|: B:H\to K\text{ linear and }\|B\|\le1\,\}.$$

Consequently, on the vector space of linear maps $H\to K$, the trace norm is
nonnegative, absolutely homogeneous, definite, and satisfies the triangle
inequality.
If $P,Q\in\mathbb C^{n\times n}$ are positive semidefinite, then $\operatorname{tr}(PQ)\ge0$ for every $n\ge0$.

For states $\rho_i$ and finite probabilities $p_i$, put $\bar\rho=\sum_i p_i\rho_i$. Then
$$0\le S(\bar\rho)-\sum_i p_iS(\rho_i)\le H(p).$$

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner product space and let $T:V\to V$
be linear. Then $T$ is normal if and only if $V$ has an orthonormal basis
consisting of eigenvectors of $T$.

derivations.claim: By [F9], $\chi_E\ge0$. Since $R<\chi_B-\chi_E$, choose $r$ with $\chi_E<r$ and $R+r<\chi_B$, and then choose $\eta>0$ so $r>\chi_E+2\eta$ and $R+r<\chi_B-2\eta$. Take $M_n=\lfloor e^{nR}\rfloor$, $L_n=\lceil e^{nr}\rceil$ and draw $M_nL_n$ independent words $X^n(m,l)$ with law $p^{\otimes n}$. For message $m$, the encoder inputs the mixed state $$\rho_{m,n}=\frac1{L_n}\sum_{l=1}^{L_n}\bigotimes_{i=1}^n\rho_{X_i(m,l)}.$$ This is a legitimate finite private randomization of the operational input state; the realized codebook is public.

For Bob use the global and conditional spectral projectors $P,Q_{x^n}$ from [[lem-it-exponential-cq-spectral-projectors]], for the receiver ensemble. Put $\Gamma_{m,l}=P Q_{X^n(m,l)}P$ and $G=\sum_{m,l}\Gamma_{m,l}$. Each $\Gamma_{m,l}$ is nonnegative and $\Gamma_{m,l}\preceq P\preceq I$. Using [F10], define $G^{-1/2}$ spectrally on $\operatorname{supp}G$ and as zero on $\ker G$, and set $\Lambda_{m,l}=G^{-1/2}\Gamma_{m,l}G^{-1/2}$ and $\Lambda_\bot=I-\Pi_{\operatorname{supp}G}$. These are nonnegative and $$\sum_{m,l}\Lambda_{m,l}+\Lambda_\bot=G^{-1/2}GG^{-1/2}+I-\Pi_{\operatorname{supp}G}=I.$$ Assign $\Lambda_\bot$ to the pair $(1,1)$; the resulting pair effects still sum to the identity, and coarsening them by $m$ gives Bob's message POVM. For each pair, the Hayashi–Nagaoka inequality [F4] with $S=\Gamma_{m,l}$ and $T=\sum_{(m',l')\ne(m,l)}\Gamma_{m',l'}$ bounds its pair-decoding error by twice its own projector failure plus four times its interference sum. The assigned failure effect only decreases the error for its designated pair. The estimate is valid without a uniform per-word projector-acceptance hypothesis: only its average is needed here. Specifically, $$\mathbb E[1-\operatorname{tr}(\Gamma_{m,l}\beta_{X^n(m,l)})]\le\varepsilon_n+2\sqrt{\varepsilon_n},$$ where $\varepsilon_n\le Ce^{-cn}$ bounds both averaged projector failures. This follows by $\operatorname{tr}(Q_xP\beta_xP)\ge\operatorname{tr}(Q_x\beta_x)-\|P\beta_xP-\beta_x\|_1$ and the gentle-measurement bound followed by Jensen. For two different independent codewords, the spectral eigenvalue and rank bounds give $$\mathbb E\operatorname{tr}(\Gamma_j\beta_{X_i^n}) =\operatorname{tr}[(P\mathbb E Q_{X_j^n}P)(P\bar\beta^{\otimes n}P)] \le e^{-n(S(\bar\beta)-\eta)}e^{n(\sum_xp_xS(\beta_x)+\eta)} =e^{-n(\chi_B-2\eta)}.$$ The equality uses the support of the first factor; the inequality uses positivity of the operator-order difference, not commutation of the two factors. Thus expected pair-error is at most $$2(\varepsilon_n+2\sqrt{\varepsilon_n})+4M_nL_ne^{-n(\chi_B-2\eta)},$$ which decays exponentially. Coarsening the pair POVM to its message label cannot increase message error.

For Eve let $P,Q_{x^n}$ denote the spectral projectors for her ensemble, put $s_E=\sum_xp_xS(\epsilon_x)$, and define $$\xi_{x^n}=P Q_{x^n}\epsilon_{x^n}Q_{x^n}P,\qquad\theta=\mathbb E\xi_{X^n}.$$ These operators satisfy $0\preceq\xi_{x^n}\preceq e^{-n(s_E-\eta)}P$, $\operatorname{tr}\xi_{x^n}\le1$, and $\operatorname{rank}P\le e^{n(S(\bar\epsilon)+\eta)}$. Their average truncation error obeys $$\mathbb E\|\epsilon_{X^n}-\xi_{X^n}\|_1\le\zeta_n:=\varepsilon_n+2\sqrt{\varepsilon_n}.$$ Indeed the conditional projector commutes with its state, so its trace-norm loss equals its failure probability. Its subnormalized output $A$ satisfies $0\preceq A\preceq\epsilon_{x^n}$, and the global-projection loss is at most $2\sqrt{\operatorname{tr}[(I-P)A]}\le2\sqrt{\operatorname{tr}[(I-P)\epsilon_{x^n}]}$. The subnormalized gentle estimate follows by applying the normalized lemma to $A/\operatorname{tr}A$ and multiplying back (the zero operator is immediate). Jensen gives the stated averaged bound.

For the $L_n$ independent words of a fixed message, centered Hilbert–Schmidt variance gives $$\mathbb E\operatorname{tr}\left[\left(\frac1{L_n}\sum_l\xi_{X^n(m,l)}-\theta\right)^2\right] =\frac1{L_n}\{\mathbb E\operatorname{tr}(\xi_{X^n}^2)-\operatorname{tr}(\theta^2)\} \le\frac{e^{-n(s_E-\eta)}}{L_n}.$$ All cross terms have zero expectation by independence. The difference is supported in $P$. Cauchy–Schwarz on singular values and Jensen imply $$\mathbb E\left\|\frac1{L_n}\sum_l\xi_{X^n(m,l)}-\theta\right\|_1\le\sqrt{\frac{e^{n(\chi_E+2\eta)}}{L_n}}.$$ Together with $\|\theta-\bar\epsilon^{\otimes n}\|_1\le\zeta_n$, this proves $$\mathbb E\left\|\tau_{m,n}-\bar\epsilon^{\otimes n}\right\|_1\le2\zeta_n+\sqrt{\frac{e^{n(\chi_E+2\eta)}}{L_n}},\qquad\tau_{m,n}=(\mathcal N^c)^{\otimes n}(\rho_{m,n}).$$ The right side decays exponentially and is independent of $m$. Consequently the expectation of the sum of average decoding error and average half-trace distance from this target decays exponentially. The codebook sample space is finite, so order the finite word/codebook alphabet and select its first deterministic codebook whose sum is at most twice its expectation (or zero if that expectation vanishes). This defines a sequence without countable choices. For that codebook let $a_n=M_n^{-1}\sum_m T(\tau_{m,n},\bar\epsilon^{\otimes n})$. The proved quantitative entropy estimate yields $$\ell_n\le2a_n n\ln\dim E+2g(a_n)\longrightarrow0.$$ This establishes the required unnormalized Holevo strong secrecy; a mere limit of trace distance without this dimension/error-rate estimate would not suffice. The average decoding error also tends to zero, while $n^{-1}\ln M_n\to R$. If the ensemble's private information is nonpositive it gives no positive lower bound; rate zero remains achievable with one message.

Let $x\mapsto\rho_x$ be a finite-input, finite-output memoryless cq channel as in [[def-it-classical-quantum-memoryless-channel]]. With the average-error code convention of [[def-it-cq-channel-block-code-and-error]], its classical capacity in nats per use is
$$C_{\rm cq}=\max_{p\in\Delta(\mathcal X)}\chi_p,\qquad \chi_p:=S\!\left(\sum_xp_x\rho_x\right)-\sum_{x:p_x>0}p_xS(\rho_x).$$
For every $0\le R<C_{\rm cq}$ a sequence of codes with rate tending to $R$ has average error tending to zero, and every reliable sequence has limiting upper rate at most $C_{\rm cq}$. This theorem concerns a fixed finite classical input alphabet and does not assert a single-letter formula for general quantum-input channels.

Let $A$ and $B$ be nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces and let $\mathcal N:\mathcal L(A)\to\mathcal L(B)$ be a quantum channel as in [[def-qc-quantum-channel]]. Choose a finite-dimensional environment $E$ and a linear isometry $V:A\to B\otimes E$ such that

$$\mathcal N(X)=\operatorname{Tr}_E(VXV^*)$$

for every $X\in\mathcal L(A)$; such a dilation exists by [[thm-qc-finite-stinespring-dilation]]. The channel

$$\mathcal N^c(X):=\operatorname{Tr}_B(VXV^*)\in\mathcal L(E)$$

is the **complementary channel associated with this chosen dilation**. The partial trace $\operatorname{Tr}_B$ contracts the first factor of the ordered product $B\otimes E$ ([[def-qc-first-factor-partial-trace]]).

It is a quantum channel: reorder $B\otimes E$ to $E\otimes B$ by the finite wire-permutation unitary ([[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]], [[thm-qc-wire-permutation-is-unitary]]); the reordered $V$ is still an isometry, so tracing its second factor $B$ gives a channel by [[thm-qc-isometry-partial-trace-is-channel]].

For a density operator $\rho$ on $A$, choose a finite purification $|\psi\rangle\in A\otimes R$ with $\operatorname{Tr}_R|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|=\rho$ ([[def-qc-ensemble-and-purification]]), and define $\omega_{BR}:=(\mathcal N\otimes\operatorname{id}_R)(|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|)$. Its **coherent information** from $A$ to $B$ is

$$I_c(\rho,\mathcal N):=S(\mathcal N(\rho))-S(\omega_{BR}),$$

where $S$ is finite-dimensional von Neumann entropy in nats ([[def-it-von-neumann-entropy]]). The value does not depend on the chosen purification: after padding reference spaces, any two purifications differ by a unitary on $R$ ([[thm-qc-purification-existence-and-unitary-equivalence]]); applying $\mathcal N\otimes\operatorname{id}_R$ preserves that unitary relation. A unitary maps an orthonormal eigenbasis to an orthonormal eigenbasis with the same eigenvalues, so entropy is unchanged ([[thm-complex-spectral-theorem-for-normal-endomorphisms]]). Padding adds only zero eigenvalues, which do not contribute.

Let $\mathcal N:A\to B$ be a finite-dimensional channel, let $V:A\to B\otimes E$ be a finite Stinespring isometry, let $\mathcal N^c(X)=\operatorname{Tr}_B(VXV^*)$, and let $\rho$ be a density operator on $A$. Then

$$I_c(\rho,\mathcal N)=S(\mathcal N(\rho))-S(\mathcal N^c(\rho)).$$

The right-hand side is independent of the chosen Stinespring dilation, since it equals the purification-defined quantity in [[def-it-quantum-channel-complement-and-coherent-information]].

Let $H,K$ be finite-dimensional complex-inner-product spaces with the tensor-product convention of [[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]]. For every $\Psi\in H\otimes K$ there are an integer $r\ge0$, positive numbers $s_1,\ldots,s_r$, and orthonormal families $u_1,\ldots,u_r\in H$ and $v_1,\ldots,v_r\in K$ such that

$$\Psi=\sum_{j=1}^r s_j u_j\otimes v_j,\qquad \|\Psi\|^2=\sum_{j=1}^r s_j^2.$$

For $\Psi=0$ take $r=0$ and the empty sum. For any chosen ordered pair of orthonormal bases, the construction below obtains the $s_j$ as the positive singular values of the coefficient matrix of $\Psi$ in their ordered product basis.

An **ordered tensor register** consists of a finite ordered list of
finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces $H_0,\ldots,H_{n-1}$, each
equipped with a specified ordered orthonormal basis. Its space is
$H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1}$, with factors retained in the displayed
order. The product basis is ordered lexicographically by its tuple of factor
indices. The empty tensor product is $\mathbb C$ with basis $\{1\}$. A
zero-dimensional factor is allowed in this mathematical construction and makes
the tensor space zero; it is not a register under
[[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]].

The inner product is linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the
second, and on elementary tensors it is

$$\left\langle\bigotimes_{k<n}x_k,\bigotimes_{k<n}y_k\right\rangle_{\otimes}:=\prod_{k<n}\langle x_k,y_k\rangle_{{\rm root},k}.$$ 

For the empty tensor, the right side is the empty product $1$, giving the
standard inner product on $\mathbb C$.

For a permutation $\sigma$ of the $n$ factor positions, the **wire permutation**
$P_\sigma$ maps the product basis vector indexed by
$(i_0,\ldots,i_{n-1})$ to the product basis vector whose output factor order is
$(\sigma(0),\ldots,\sigma(n-1))$. It is extended linearly; for $n=0$ it is the
identity on $\mathbb C$. The extension is a linear map in the sense of
[[def-linear-map]].

Let $X$ be a finite nonempty classical label set, represented by a register $H_X$ with computational orthonormal basis $(\xi_x)_{x\in X}$ ([[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]]). For each $x$, write $\Pi_xz:=\langle z,\xi_x\rangle\xi_x$, the rank-one orthogonal projection using the root linear-first convention, as in [[lem-it-finite-cq-block-sum-is-a-state]]. Let $H_B$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space. A finite **classical-quantum state** is

$$\rho_{XB}:=\sum_{x\in X}p_x\Pi_x\otimes\rho_x,$$

where $p_x\ge0$, $\sum_xp_x=1$, and each $\rho_x$ is a density operator on $H_B$. It is a density operator by [[lem-it-finite-cq-block-sum-is-a-state]]. Its quantum marginal is $\bar\rho_B:=\sum_xp_x\rho_x=\operatorname{Tr}_X\rho_{XB}$ by the second-factor partial-trace formula in [[def-qc-partial-trace]], and it is a density operator by [[lem-it-partial-traces-of-a-state-are-states]]. The **Holevo information** of this ensemble is

$$\chi(\{p_x,\rho_x\}_{x\in X}):=S(\bar\rho_B)-\sum_{x:p_x>0}p_xS(\rho_x),$$

where zero-probability branches contribute nothing. This is measured in nats under [[def-it-von-neumann-entropy]].

The function $\log:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ is continuous and strictly increasing, is onto $\mathbb R$, and satisfies, for $x,y>0$,
$$\log(xy)=\log x+\log y,\qquad \log(x/y)=\log x-\log y,\qquad \log(1/x)=-\log x.$$
Also $\log 1=0$.

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner product space and let $T:V\to V$
be linear. Then $T$ is normal if and only if $V$ has an orthonormal basis
consisting of eigenvectors of $T$.

Let $H,K$ be finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces with $d=\dim K\ge1$, and fix an ordered orthonormal basis $e_0,\ldots,e_{d-1}$ of $K$. Let $X e_j=e_{j+1\,\mathrm{mod}\,d}$ and $Z e_j=\omega^j e_j$, where $\omega=\exp(2\pi i/d)$ (and $\omega=1$ when $d=1$). For $R\in\operatorname{End}(H\otimes K)$,
$$\frac1{d^2}\sum_{p,q=0}^{d-1}(I_H\otimes X^pZ^q)R(I_H\otimes X^pZ^q)^\dagger=(\operatorname{Tr}_K R)\otimes I_K/d.$$

derivations.claim: Fix a $D$-dimensional subspace of the input, with embedding $J$ and flat state $\tau=JJ^*/D$. Share $|\Phi_D\rangle$ between the sender's subspace and a receiver reference $R$. On the sender half apply the $D^2$ Weyl unitaries, each uniformly likely, before the input embedding. The Weyl matrices in the fixed ordered basis are $U_{ab}|j\rangle=e^{2\pi i bj/D}|j+a\pmod D\rangle$. Reorder the shared state as $R\otimes\mathbb C^D$ using [F5]. Applying [F9] with retained factor $R$ and twirled factor the sender's $D$-dimensional register gives $I_R/D\otimes I_D/D$, since the retained marginal is $I_R/D$. Reordering back gives $I_D/D\otimes I_R/D$. The supplied finite root-of-unity calculation establishes the phase cancellation for every $D\ge1$.

Let $\sigma_{ab}$ be the joint output on $B R$ of this finite cq alphabet through $\mathcal N$. Because $(U_{ab}\otimes I)|\Phi_D\rangle=(I\otimes U_{ab}^T)|\Phi_D\rangle$ in coefficient coordinates, all $\sigma_{ab}$ are related by a unitary on $R$ and have identical entropy $S(\mathcal N^c(\tau))$ by purity of the full Stinespring output and [F4]. Their average is $\mathcal N(\tau)\otimes I_R/D$. The spectral theorem [F8] and logarithm law [F7] give $S(\mathcal N(\tau)\otimes I_R/D)=S(\mathcal N(\tau))+\ln D$. Thus [F6] gives the ensemble Holevo information exactly as $$\chi=\ln D+S(\mathcal N(\tau))-S(\mathcal N^c(\tau))=f_{\mathcal N}(\tau).$$ The HSW theorem applies to this fixed finite cq channel $ab\mapsto\sigma_{ab}$, with output $B R$. Each cq codeword is physically implemented by its sequence of Weyl operations on independent shared maximally entangled pairs. Its collective POVM is a permitted receiver measurement and its rate/error are exactly those of HSW. Therefore every nonnegative rate strictly below $f_{\mathcal N}(\tau)$ is entanglement-assisted achievable. Dimension $D=1$ is included: the one-letter ensemble then has Holevo information zero.

Every density operator $\rho$ on a nonzero finite-dimensional complex-inner-product space $H$ has a purification on some finite-dimensional auxiliary space. More precisely, if $r=\operatorname{rank}(\rho)$, it has one on an auxiliary space of dimension $r$. If $\Psi_i\in H\otimes K_i$ ($i=1,2$) are any two purifications of the same $\rho$, then for every integer $m\ge\max(\dim K_1,\dim K_2)$ and every pair of linear isometric embeddings $\iota_i:K_i\to\mathbb C^m$, where $\mathbb C^m$ has its standard complex inner product, there is a unitary $U$ on $\mathbb C^m$ such that

$$ (I_H\otimes U)(I_H\otimes\iota_2)\Psi_2=(I_H\otimes\iota_1)\Psi_1. $$

linear maps $H\to H$ ([[def-linear-map]]).

$$\bigl(\operatorname{Tr}_B(R)\bigr)_{i i'}:=\sum_{j<b}R_{(i,j),(i',j)}.$$

Rows are output coordinates and columns are input coordinates, as in
[[def-coordinate-column-and-matrix-of-a-linear-map]]. If $b=0$, the sum is
empty and equals $0$. The notation $\operatorname{Tr}_B$ means that the second
factor is contracted; the first factor and its order are retained.

Let $H_0,\ldots,H_{n-1}$ be a finite ordered list of finite-dimensional
complex inner-product spaces with specified ordered orthonormal bases of
sizes $d_0,\ldots,d_{n-1}$, allowing $d_k=0$. The elementary tensors of the
factor bases, ordered lexicographically, form an orthonormal basis of the

$$\dim(H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1})=\prod_{k<n}d_k.$$

For the empty list the product is $1$ and the tensor space is $\mathbb C$; if
any $d_k=0$, the tensor space is zero and the product basis is empty.

Let $H$ and $K$ be finite-dimensional (have finite bases by [[def-dimension]])
complex inner-product spaces. A
**quantum channel** from $H$ to $K$ is a complex-linear map
$\Phi:\mathcal L(H)\to\mathcal L(K)$ ([[def-linear-map]]) that is completely
positive ([[def-qc-completely-positive-map]]) and trace-preserving, meaning

$$\operatorname{tr}(\Phi(X))=\operatorname{tr}(X)\qquad\text{for every }X\in\mathcal L(H),$$

where trace is the basis-independent trace of a finite-dimensional
endomorphism ([[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]). Trace preservation is
required on the full operator space, not only on density operators. This
definition is mathematical and assumes no physical realization.

Let $H,K,E$ be finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces and let
$V:H\to K\otimes E$ be a linear isometry. Then
$$\Phi(X)=\operatorname{Tr}_E(VXV^\dagger),\qquad X\in\mathcal L(H),$$
is a quantum channel from $H$ to $K$.
Every finite-dimensional real or complex inner product space has an orthonormal basis. In dimension zero, this is the empty basis.

If $W$ is a subspace of a finite-dimensional real or complex inner product space $V$, then

$$V=W\oplus W^\perp.$$

Thus every $v\in V$ has unique vectors $w\in W$ and $z\in W^\perp$ with $v=w+z$.

Let $F$ be a field ([[def-field]]), let $n \in \mathbb{N}$, let $V$ be a vector
space over $F$ ([[def-vector-space]]) and let $U$ be a family of linear subspaces
$U_i$ of $V$ indexed by $i < n$ ([[def-linear-subspace]],
[[def-sum-of-linear-subspaces]]) with

$$V \;=\; \bigoplus_{i<n} U_i$$

([[def-internal-direct-sum]]) and every $U_i$ finite-dimensional over $F$
([[def-dimension]]). Then $V$ is finite-dimensional over $F$ and

$$\dim_F V \;=\; \sum_{i<n} \dim_F U_i ,$$

the right-hand side being the finite sum of [[def-monoid-finite-product]] read
additively in the commutative monoid $(\mathbb{N}, +, 0)$
([[def-nat-addition]], [[lem-nat-add-identity]],
[[lem-nat-add-associative]], [[lem-nat-add-commutative]]).

**The base case is a genuine case.** At $n = 0$ the direct sum of the empty
family is $\{0_V\}$ and the empty sum of natural numbers is $0$, so the formula
reads $\dim_F\{0_V\} = 0$. **At $n = 2$** it reads
$\dim_F(U \oplus W) = \dim_F U + \dim_F W$.

**No choice principle is used.** The only inputs are
[[thm-dimension-formula]] and [[thm-dimension-of-a-linear-subspace]], both of
which are proved in finite dimension without one.

derivations.claim: Choose a finite purification $|\Omega\rangle_{ZAF}$ of $\omega_{ZA}$ by [F1] and reorder its factors as $A(ZF)$. Let $\rho_A=\sum_{j=1}^r\lambda_j|a_j\rangle\langle a_j|$ be a spectral decomposition on its positive support, obtained from [F7]. Expand each purification in the product basis using this same eigenbasis on $A$: $$|\psi\rangle_{RA}=\sum_{j=1}^r|r_j^0\rangle_R|a_j\rangle_A,\qquad |\Omega\rangle_{A(ZF)}=\sum_{j=1}^r|a_j\rangle_A|z_j^0\rangle_{ZF}.$$ The partial-trace coordinate formula [F2] and the fact that both $A$ marginals equal $\rho_A$ show that the coefficient vectors have Gram matrices $\langle r_j^0,r_k^0\rangle=\lambda_j\delta_{jk}$ and $\langle z_j^0,z_k^0\rangle=\lambda_j\delta_{jk}$. Thus $|r_j\rangle:=|r_j^0\rangle/\sqrt{\lambda_j}$ and $|z_j\rangle:=|z_j^0\rangle/\sqrt{\lambda_j}$ are orthonormal and $$|\psi\rangle_{RA}=\sum_{j=1}^r\sqrt{\lambda_j}|r_j\rangle_R|a_j\rangle_A,\qquad |\Omega\rangle_{A(ZF)}=\sum_{j=1}^r\sqrt{\lambda_j}|a_j\rangle_A|z_j\rangle_{ZF}.$$ This coefficient argument also handles repeated positive eigenvalues because the chosen basis is fixed before either expansion.

Let $d=\dim R=\dim A$. In every case set $G=\mathbb C^d$, fix its first coordinate unit vector $|0\rangle_G$, and append it to $|\Omega\rangle$. Since $Z$ and the purifying space $F$ are nonzero, $\dim(Z\otimes F\otimes G)\ge d$. Denote the resulting orthonormal Schmidt partners by $|z_j'\rangle=|z_j\rangle|0\rangle_G$. The map $U_0:\operatorname{span}\{|r_j\rangle}\to\operatorname{span}\{|z_j'\rangle\}$ given by $U_0|r_j\rangle=|z_j'\rangle$ is an isometry. Extend $\{|r_j\rangle\}$ to an orthonormal basis of $R$ and choose the same number of additional orthonormal vectors in the orthogonal complement of the $z_j'$ in $Z\otimes F\otimes G$; [F5] and the target dimension bound ensure this is possible. Sending the added basis vectors to those target vectors extends $U_0$ to a linear isometry $U:R\to Z\otimes F\otimes G$ on all of $R$. By construction, $(U\otimes I_A)|\psi\rangle$ is exactly the padded purification $|\Omega\rangle\otimes|0\rangle_G$, after reordering to $Z(F\otimes G)A$. This construction includes the singular case $r<d$, since it extends $U$ on all zero-Schmidt directions of $R$.

Define $\Lambda(X)=\operatorname{Tr}_{F\otimes G}(UXU^*)$ from $\mathcal L(R)$ to $\mathcal L(Z)$. Since $U$ is an isometry, [F4] makes $\Lambda$ completely positive and trace-preserving on the full operator space. Applying it to the reference factor of $|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|$ traces $F\otimes G$ from the pure state $|(U\otimes I_A)\psi\rangle\langle(U\otimes I_A)\psi|$, leaving its $ZA$ marginal, which is $\omega_{ZA}$ by construction and is unchanged by the appended pure $G$ register [F6]. Thus $(\Lambda\otimes\operatorname{id}_A)(|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|)=\omega_{ZA}$, as required.
